items.body:
# Bug Report: Hermes Desktop drops intermediate assistant messages in multi-message turns

## Summary
On Hermes **Desktop** (v0.16.0), when a single agent turn produces **multiple
assistant text messages interleaved with tool calls**, the Desktop UI only
renders the LAST assistant message of the turn. The earlier assistant text
messages are correctly **saved to state.db** but never shown (or are shown
briefly then replaced/collapsed). To the user this looks like "the response
changed into something else" or "my answer disappeared" — a serious trust issue,
because substantive content the agent actually produced becomes invisible.

This is NOT a reasoning/thinking-vs-final swap (my first wrong theory). It is
intermediate **content** messages being dropped from the render.

## Environment
- Hermes Agent **v0.16.0 (2026.6.5)**, build 56236b16
- Interface: **Desktop app** (Windows 10, AMD64)
- Python 3.11.15, OpenAI SDK 2.24.0
- Model: anthropic/claude-opus-4.8 via openrouter
- Relevant config: `display.streaming: true`, `display.show_reasoning: true`,
  `display.final_response_markdown: render`, `display.interim_assistant_messages: true`

## Evidence (ground truth from state.db)
Session `20260606_185548_6e5c26`. ONE user turn (msg 507) produced this saved
sequence — all at near-identical timestamps (one turn):

| id  | role      | tool     | content chars |
|-----|-----------|----------|---------------|

items.body:
## Feature Request: Board-level kanban event subscription

### Problem

`hermes kanban notify-subscribe` is **per-task only** — every dispatched card requires a separate manual subscription. In real multi-agent workflows (epoch-driven-convergence, fan-out dispatch, parallel exploration), orchestrators routinely dispatch 10-20+ cards at once. Subscribing each one is:

- **Impractical** (16+ subscriptions, all per-task-id)
- **Error-prone** (orchestrator forgets; reports task done 12+ min late)
- **At odds with the existing event-stream** (`hermes kanban watch` works board-wide, why not notify?)

### Use Case

```bash
# Today (per-task, 16 lines):
for id in $(hermes kanban list --json | jq -r '.[] | select(.status=="ready") | .id'); do
  hermes kanban notify-subscribe "$id" --platform feishu --chat-id <home>
done

# Desired (board-wide, 1 line):
hermes kanban notify-subscribe --board lq-charset-fix \
  --kinds completed,blocked,crashed \
  --platform feishu --chat-id <home>
```

### Proposed API

Three options, in order of preference:

**Option A: Board-level subscribe** (mirrors `hermes kanban boards switch`)
```bash
hermes kanban notify-subscribe --board <slug> --kinds X \
  --platform feishu --chat-id <home>
```

**Option B: Running-all subscribe** (subscribes to currently-running tasks, persists state)
```bash
hermes kanban notify-subscribe --all-running --kinds X --platform ...
```

**Option C: Auto-subscribe on create** (opt-in flag, not breaking)
```bash
hermes kanban create "..." --auto-notify feishu:home
```

### Why now

Hit this concretely on 2026-06-07 during a 16-card fan-out (LQ charset fix epoch 2). I had to choose between:
1. Manually `notify-subscribe` 16 times → fragile, forgot
2. Background `kanban watch` + `notify_on_complete` → works, but `notify_on_complete` itself has bug #6718

Even after #6718 lands, board-level subscribe is still needed for ergonomics.

### Workaround

Documented in skill `kanban-aware-dispatch`: 3-layer fallback
1. Per-task `notify-subscribe` (works but tedious)
2. `hermes kanban watch --kinds X` in background + `notify_on_complete` (real event stream, 0.5s)
3. Cron + custom watcher script (every 2m, silent when no change)

### Related

- Issue #6718 (background process notifications not delivering) — PR has fix, not yet merged
- Skill: `kanban-aware-dispatch` (proposed, in user's local ~/.hermes/skills/)
- Docs: `hermes-agent` skill §Durable & Background Systems → Kanban

## Summary

On macOS, the Hermes Dock icon appears visibly larger than neighboring normal app icons after updating to the current desktop build.

## Current behavior

The desktop main process currently resolves the Dock/window icon from `apple-touch-icon.png` assets:

```js
const APP_ICON_PATHS = [
  path.join(APP_ROOT, 'public', 'apple-touch-icon.png'),
  path.join(APP_ROOT, 'dist', 'apple-touch-icon.png'),
  path.join(unpackedPathFor(APP_ROOT), 'dist', 'apple-touch-icon.png')
]
```

The current icon artwork nearly fills the full square canvas. Measured alpha bounding boxes after a fresh update:

```text
apps/desktop/assets/icon.png
  1024x1024, alpha bbox (39, 38, 975, 955), visible ratio ~= 0.914
apps/desktop/public/apple-touch-icon.png
  1254x1254, alpha bbox (48, 47, 1194, 1169), visible ratio ~= 0.914
apps/desktop/dist/apple-touch-icon.png
  1254x1254, alpha bbox (48, 47, 1194, 1169), visible ratio ~= 0.914
/Applications/Hermes.app/Contents/Resources/icon.icns
  1024x1024, alpha bbox (39, 38, 975, 955), visible ratio ~= 0.914
```

As a visual reference, common macOS Dock icons on the same machine measure closer to ~0.84 visible ratio for their rounded-square/squircle footprint:

```text
Telegram/Safari: ~= 0.844
Bilibili: ~= 0.81
```

So Hermes looks oversized in the Dock compared with adjacent apps.

## Expected behavior

Hermes should use a macOS-appropriate icon asset with normal Dock-safe padding, so its visible footprint matches other macOS app icons.

A likely fix would be to:

1. Normalize the macOS icon artwork so the rounded-square silhouette uses roughly the same visual footprint as standard macOS app icons.
2. Avoid using `apple-touch-icon.png` as the primary macOS Dock icon, or make sure that file is also normalized if it remains a fallback.
3. Prefer a packaged real filesystem resource such as `process.resourcesPath/icon.png` or a valid `.icns` asset for `app.dock.setIcon()`.

## Related startup robustness note

While experimenting locally, using an `.icns` path directly caused Electron to throw during startup on one build:

```text
Failed to load image from path '/Applications/Hermes.app/Contents/Resources/icon.icns'
UnhandledPromiseRejectionWarning: Error: Failed to load image from path ... icon.icns
    at createWindow (.../app.asar/electron/main.cjs:4630:17)
```

That left the Hermes window blank because the icon load failure interrupted window creation. It would be good for the icon resolution path to verify `nativeImage.createFromPath(...).isEmpty()` or otherwise guard `app.dock.setIcon()` so a bad icon asset cannot break app startup.

## Environment

```text
macOS desktop app
Hermes.app CFBundleShortVersionString: 0.15.1
hermes-agent commit: 40cea4d58
```

items.title: ScoutGate v2: bind /goal authority to lifecycle leases, epochs, and manifests

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Problem

`/goal` currently has useful operational state, but that state is mechanical controller state only. It must not be treated as approval, safety, or mutation authority.

ScoutGate v2 needs a source-grounded `/goal` authority lifecycle so queued kickoff/continuation work cannot be made authoritative by stale persistence, telemetry, status messages, subagent output, or hook-side evidence.

## Current ground truth

- `GoalState` persists goal/status/turn/judge fields, but does not carry lifecycle id, controller id, lease/epoch/fencing token, manifest digest, retry group/attempt index, or a current-lifecycle authority anchor.
- `GoalManager.evaluate_after_turn()` returns operational progress decisions, not authority.
- Gateway continuation freshness currently only re-checks whether the goal is active; it does not bind lifecycle id, epoch, digest, retry group, session lineage, or controller lease.
- Existing plugin hooks can block tool calls after the fact, but they cannot safely own `/goal` lifecycle authority or queued continuation freshness.

## Required design split

- Mechanical state: `/goal` SessionDB state and kickoff/continuation queues.
- Evidence: judge output, subagent reviews, runner artifacts, status/telemetry, hook observations.
- Authority anchors: lifecycle manifest, controller lease/epoch, fencing token, digests, retry group, attempt index, session lineage binding.
- Minted decision: only the active current-lifecycle `/goal` controller can mint an authoritative ScoutGate decision.

## Minimal implementation sequence

1. Add a core `/goal` lifecycle state model: lifecycle id, controller id, lease/epoch/fencing, manifest digest, retry group/attempt index, session lineage binding.
2. Centralize `/goal` lifecycle APIs so CLI, gateway, and TUI use the same authority path.
3. Strengthen queued continuation freshness before continuations run.
4. Add a ScoutGate policy module for schemas, semantic validation, reason codes, fixture corpus, and UX/status wording.
5. Use hooks only for secondary enforcement/audit; hooks may block unsafe tools when no valid current-lifecycle decision exists, but must not mint authority.

## Related issues

- #27777 — goal lifecycle plugin hooks.
- #34197 — stale continuation/compression amplification.
- #33618 and #18467 — `/goal` lost across compression/session rotation.
- #30577 — structured `/goal` status metadata.

## Non-authorizing boundary

This issue is a design/implementation ledger. It does not authorize mutation, runner contact, config/profile/gateway changes, PR merge, issue closure, or live enablement. Each implementation slice still needs an exact approval/validation gate.

items.title: WSL: Desktop app cannot use Windows IME (input method) - workaround using remote backend

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Problem

When running `hermes desktop` on WSL2 (Windows 11 with WSLg), the Electron app window displays correctly, but **Windows system input methods (e.g., Microsoft Pinyin) do not work** in the app. Users cannot type Chinese or other non-ASCII characters.

## Environment
- WSL2 on Windows 11 (build 26200)
- WSLg enabled (Wayland + XWayland)
- Hermes Agent (git main branch)
- Electron 40.9.3 (Chrome 144)
- Running as root in WSL

## Root Cause

WSLg's RDP-based Weston compositor does not properly forward Windows IME events to Linux GUI applications. This affects both:
- **X11 mode** (`--ozone-platform=x11`): XIM protocol doesn't receive Windows IME input
- **Wayland mode** (`--ozone-platform=wayland`): text-input-v3 protocol doesn't work with WSLg's Weston 9.0.0

We tried multiple approaches:
1. `--enable-wayland-ime` flag - no effect
2. `--wayland-text-input-version=1` and `=3` - no effect
3. Installing/configuring ibus and fcitx5 in WSL - these are Linux IME frameworks, they can't bridge to Windows IME
4. Various Electron flags (`--disable-gpu`, `--in-process-gpu`, etc.) - fixed GPU crashes but not IME

## Workaround: Windows Native Electron + WSL Backend

Build a Windows version of the Electron app and connect it to the WSL backend:

### Step 1: Build Windows version from WSL
```bash
cd /usr/local/lib/hermes-agent/apps/desktop
npx cross-env NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=16384 electron-builder --dir --win
```

### Step 2: Copy to Windows
```bash
cp -r apps/desktop/release/win-unpacked /mnt/c/Users/<username>/Hermes-Desktop/
```

### Step 3: Start dashboard with session token
```bash
export HERMES_DASHBOARD_SESSION_TOKEN=$(python3 -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))")
hermes dashboard --host 0.0.0.0 --no-open --port 9119 --insecure
```

### Step 4: Create Windows launcher (Hermes-Desktop.bat)
```batch
@echo off
cd /d C:\Users\<username>\Hermes-Desktop
set HERMES_DESKTOP_REMOTE_URL=http://localhost:9119
set HERMES_DESKTOP_REMOTE_TOKEN=<session_token>
start "" "C:\Users\<username>\Hermes-Desktop\Hermes.exe"
```

## Additional Issues Found

1. **Root user + Electron**: Requires `--no-sandbox` flag
2. **GPU crash in WSL**: Requires `--disable-gpu --disable-software-rasterizer --in-process-gpu` flags
3. **Python output buffering**: `print()` messages in `cmd_gui()` are buffered and not visible when Electron subprocess starts

## Suggestion

Consider adding built-in support for:
1. Detecting WSL and automatically applying the necessary flags
2. A `hermes desktop --remote <url>` option to connect to a remote backend
3. Better documentation for WSL users about the IME limitation and workaround

## Problem

When a Hermes agent encounters an HTTP 402 Payment Required response from a paid API, it has no way to resolve it. The agent fails silently or returns an error to the user.

HTTP 402 was designed for exactly this — machine-to-machine payments. With the rise of paid AI APIs, agents need a native payment capability.

## Proposed Solution

A **Mag3nt payment plugin** for Hermes Agent that automatically detects and settles HTTP 402 challenges using USDC virtual cards.

### Plugin structure

```
~/.hermes/plugins/mag3nt-pay/
├── plugin.yaml
├── __init__.py
├── schemas.py
└── tools.py
```

### What it does

1. Agent hits a 402 response → plugin activates
2. Detects payment protocol (x402, MPP, AP2, or Pay Link)
3. Checks the agent's card balance
4. Settles payment via `POST https://mag3nt.com/api/pay`
5. Retries the original request with the receipt

### What Mag3nt provides

- **Virtual card issuance** via API — no human intervention
- **USDC payments** on Base, Solana, and most EVMs
- **Settlement** on Solana, Base, and Tempo
- **Spend controls** — per-card limits, MCC locks, single-use cards, expiry
- **One universal endpoint** — auto-detects payment protocol, settles on-chain

### Tool schema (for the LLM)

```python
{
    "name": "mag3nt_pay",
    "description": "Pay for any API that returns HTTP 402 using USDC",
    "parameters": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
            "url": {"type": "string", "description": "The 402-protected URL to pay"},
            "method": {"type": "string", "default": "POST"},
            "body": {"type": "object", "description": "Request body for the API call"}
        },
        "required": ["url"]
    }
}
```

## Already available

- **Python SDK:** [mag3nt on PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/mag3nt/)
- **npm SDK:** [@mag3nt/sdk](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@mag3nt/sdk)
- **OpenClaw skill:** [mag3nt-pay on ClawHub](https://clawhub.ai/skills/mag3nt-pay)
- **Source:** [mag3nt-com/openclaw-skill](https://github.com/mag3nt-com/openclaw-skill)
- **API docs:** [docs.mag3nt.com](https://docs.mag3nt.com)
- **Live platform:** [mag3nt.com](https://mag3nt.com)

## Why this matters for Hermes

- HTTP 402 is becoming the standard for paid AI APIs
- Hermes agents calling external tools will increasingly hit paywalls
- A payment plugin makes Hermes agents truly autonomous — they can acquire resources without human intervention
- Mag3nt is MIT licensed with a free tier

Happy to build and submit the plugin as a PR. Would love feedback on the approach.

### Bug Description

The documentation says per-model `supports_vision` under `custom_providers[*].models[*]` is honored for native image routing, but `agent/image_routing.py` does not currently read that section.

With `agent.image_input_mode: auto`, a vision-capable named custom provider model can still route image attachments through the text/`vision_analyze` path instead of attaching images natively to the main model.

This is visible in the latest release tag `v2026.6.5` as well as my installed `v0.15.1 (2026.5.29)` build.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a named custom provider with per-model vision metadata:

```yaml
model:
  default: mimoanth/mimo-v2.5
  provider: custom:9router-anthropic

agent:
  image_input_mode: auto

custom_providers:
  - name: 9router-anthropic
    base_url: http://127.0.0.1:20128
    api_mode: anthropic_messages
    models:
      mimoanth/mimo-v2.5:
        context_length: 1048576
        supports_vision: true
```

2. Send an image attachment through a gateway/chat path, or evaluate the routing decision with the loaded config:

```python
from hermes_cli.config import load_config
from agent.auxiliary_client import _read_main_provider, _read_main_model
from agent.image_routing import decide_image_input_mode, _lookup_supports_vision

cfg = load_config()
p = _read_main_provider()
m = _read_main_model()
print(_lookup_supports_vision(p, m, cfg))
print(decide_image_input_mode(p, m, cfg))
```

3. Observe that the custom provider per-model `supports_vision: true` is not used by `image_routing.py`.

### Expected Behavior

In `agent.image_input_mode: auto`, if the active model is declared with `custom_providers[*].models[model_id].supports_vision: true`, image attachments should be routed natively to the main model.

This would match the provider documentation, which says the same key is honored on per-named-provider models.

### Actual Behavior

The route stays on the text pre-analysis path unless `model.supports_vision: true` or `providers.<provider>.models.<model>.supports_vision: true` is configured.

In environments without an auxiliary vision provider configured, this can surface as:

```text
No LLM provider configured for task=vision provider=auto. Run: hermes setup
```

Even though the active custom provider model has `supports_vision: true` under `custom_providers[].models`.

### Affected Component

Configuration (config.yaml, .env, hermes setup)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A (CLI only)

### Debug Report

```shell
Not run. This report is based on static source/config inspection and a minimal local routing check. I did not upload debug output because config/log bundles may contain provider endpoints, API keys, or private conversation data.

Local environment checked:
- macOS 15.7.7
- Python 3.11.15
- Installed version: v0.15.1 (2026.5.29), commit 9af54b2f8c0e
- Latest release checked: v2026.6.5 / v0.16.0

Latest release source still shows the same routing logic in `agent/image_routing.py`.
```

### Operating System

macOS 15.7.7 (24G720)

### Python Version

Python 3.11.15

### Hermes Version

Hermes Agent v0.15.1 (2026.5.29); latest checked v0.16.0 / v2026.6.5

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell
No runtime traceback is required to identify this. The mismatch is visible in source:

- `agent/image_routing.py::_supports_vision_override` checks `model.supports_vision` and `providers.<provider>.models.<model>.supports_vision`.
- It does not check `custom_providers[*].models[*].supports_vision`.
- The docs state that `custom_providers[*].models[*].supports_vision` is honored.
```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

Root cause appears to be in `agent/image_routing.py::_supports_vision_override`.

Current resolution order in `v2026.6.5`:

1. `model.supports_vision`
2. `providers.<provider>.models.<model>.supports_vision`
3. fallback to models.dev

There is no lookup for the legacy/list-style named custom provider schema:

```yaml
custom_providers:
  - name: my-provider
    models:
      my-model:
        supports_vision: true
```

That makes the documentation and runtime behavior inconsistent.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Extend `_supports_vision_override()` to also inspect `custom_providers` entries after the top-level and `providers` checks.

Suggested behavior:

- read `cfg.get("custom_providers")` when it is a list
- match entries by `name` against `model.provider` after stripping a leading `custom:`, and against runtime provider values like `custom:<name>`
- read `entry["models"][model]["supports_vision"]`
- pass the value through the same `_coerce_capability_bool()` helper

A regression test should cover `custom_providers[].models.<model>.supports_vision: true` causing `decide_image_input_mode(..., auto)` to return `native`.

name: Bug report
     about: pre_tool_call plugin hook cannot block/intercept web_search tool calls
     title: "[Bug] pre_tool_call plugin hook returns discarded — cannot block or redirect tool calls"                  
     labels: bug
     assignees: ''
     Bug Description

     When a plugin registers a pre_tool_call hook via ctx.register_hook("pre_tool_call", handler), the return value
     from the handler is discarded by the agent loop. This makes it impossible for plugins to intercept, block, or
     redirect tool calls — despite the documentation stating:                                                          

     > "Plugins that need to enforce policy (rate limiting, security restrictions, approval workflows) can return
     {"action": "block", "message": "..."} from their pre_tool_call callback."
     Environment

     - Hermes Agent version: v0.16.0
     - Profile: stock (via Telegram gateway)
     - Platform: Telegram
     - Python: 3.11+
     Steps to Reproduce

     1. Create a plugin at ~/.hermes/plugins/test-intercept/ with:
     python
     def register(ctx):
         ctx.register_hook("pre_tool_call", handler)

     def handler(kwargs):
         return {"action": "block", "message": "Blocked by policy"}

     2. In Telegram, ask the agent to run web_search for any query
     3. Observe that the agent still executes web_search successfully — the block directive is ignored                 
     Root Cause

     The get_pre_tool_call_block_message() function in hermes_cli/plugins.py (line 1666) calls
     invoke_hook("pre_tool_call", ...) to collect hook return values. However, invoke_hook() internally calls
     HookRegistry.emit(), which discards all return values**.

     The HookRegistry class (in hermes_cli/hooks.py) has both:
     - emit() — fires handlers, discards returns (used for observe-only hooks)                                         
     - emit_collect() — fires handlers and collects return values (used for decision hooks)                            

     But invoke_hook() uses emit(), not emit_collect(). This means all pre_tool_call hook return values are
     silently discarded before get_pre_tool_call_block_message() can inspect them.
     Expected Behavior

     A pre_tool_call hook that returns {"action": "block", "message": "..."} should block the tool call and display
     the message. The agent should not execute the blocked tool.
     Suggested Fix

     In hermes_cli/hooks.py, change the invoke_hook() function to use emit_collect() instead of emit() for the
     pre_tool_call event type. This way, return values from plugin hooks are captured and can be used by
     get_pre_tool_call_block_message() to enforce blocking policies.
     Related Issues

     - #359 — Enhanced Extension System with Tool Interception & Lifecycle Hooks                                       
     - #26568 — Hermes Agent ignoring hot memory and using disabled tools                                              
     - #17309 — WEB tools not being disabled even after disabling                                                      
     Additional Context

     This bug affects any plugin that needs to intercept web_search/web_extract for security, compliance, or
     rate-limiting purposes. In our case, we needed to block web_search for overseas horse racing queries to

## Summary

Two related CLI usability issues encountered in a corporate network environment (China intranet with restricted outbound access to github.com and external APIs).

### Issue 1: `hermes skills browse` / `hermes skills search` hang indefinitely on network timeout

**Environment:** Corporate intranet with no direct access to github.com:443, skills.sh, clawhub.ai, and other external skill registries.

**Reproduction:**
```bash
hermes skills search "github" --limit 3
# Hangs indefinitely (30+ seconds), no output, no timeout feedback to user

hermes skills browse
# Same behavior - hangs with no feedback
```

**Expected:** Should timeout gracefully within a reasonable time (e.g. 10-15s) and show partial results or a clear error message. `--source official` works fine since those skills are local.

**Workaround:** Use `--source official` to only search local bundled skills.

**Notes:** I see there are related open issues (#37267, #40650) addressing timeout handling, but the user-facing behavior in v0.16.0 is still a silent hang with no progress indicator. In restricted network environments this makes the skills hub completely unusable without the `--source` workaround.

### Issue 2: `hermes update` intermittent session-resume misrouting

**Environment:** macOS 26.5.1, Hermes v0.16.0 (upstream 846821d8), installed via git clone + install script.

**Symptom:** Running `hermes update` (bare, no flags) was intermittently treated as a session resume rather than the update subcommand. The wrapper script (`~/.local/bin/hermes`) passes `"$@"` directly to the venv hermes binary:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
unset PYTHONPATH
unset PYTHONHOME
exec "/Users/zhytao/.hermes-agent/venv/bin/hermes" "$@"
```

Adding `--` before `"$@"` in the exec line fixed the misrouting:
```bash
exec "..." -- "$@"
```

However, after upgrading to v0.16.0, `hermes update` without `--` now works correctly most of the time. The root cause may be an argparse edge case where the positional argument handling interacts with session name resolution in `_coalesce_session_name_args()`.

**Note:** This may have been partially fixed in v0.16.0 but I'm reporting it since it was a real issue we hit in production use and the wrapper `--` workaround was needed for v0.15.1.

## Environment

- **Hermes:** v0.16.0 (upstream 846821d8)
- **OS:** macOS 26.5.1 (Apple Silicon)
- **Python:** 3.11.15
- **Install method:** git clone + install script
- **Network:** Corporate intranet, github.com:443 requires proxy/VPN
- **Token auth:** `ghp_` classic PAT with `repo` scope

## Suggested Improvements

1. **Skills hub timeout UX:** Add a progress indicator and hard timeout (15s default) for external registry searches. Show "Searching official skills... (external registries timed out)" rather than silent hang.
2. **Wrapper script:** Consider adding `--` by default in the generated wrapper to prevent argparse ambiguity between subcommands and positional args.

items.title: fix(plugins): `hermes plugins list` does not discover nested category plugins

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Bug Description

`hermes_cli/plugins_cmd.py:_discover_all_plugins()` only iterates **immediate subdirectories** of `~/.hermes/plugins/` and the bundled `plugins/` directory. It does **not** recurse into nested category directories (e.g. `plugins/web/<name>/`, `plugins/image_gen/<name>/`, `plugins/browser/<name>/`).

This means:

- **All bundled category plugins** (`web/tavily`, `web/exa`, `web-parallel`, `image_gen/openai`, `browser/browser_use`, `video_gen/fal`, etc.) are **invisible** to `hermes plugins list` — they do not appear in the table, plain, or JSON output.
- **User-installed category plugins** (e.g. `~/.hermes/plugins/web/tinyfish/`) load correctly at runtime via `PluginManager._scan_directory()` but are **invisible** to the CLI listing.
- `hermes plugins enable/disable <name>` uses a different code path (`_plugin_exists`) that does iterate all subdirs, so enabling works — but the plugin still never appears in the list.

The root cause is that `_discover_all_plugins()` does a flat `iterdir()` + `continue` on dirs without `plugin.yaml`, while the runtime scanner (`PluginManager._scan_directory_level` in `hermes_cli/plugins.py:1227`) correctly recurses into category directories up to 2 levels deep.

## Impact

- **12 bundled plugins** invisible to `hermes plugins list`: all `web/*` (brave-free, ddgs, exa, firecrawl, parallel, searxng, tavily, xai), `image_gen/*` (openai, fal, krea, openai-codex, xai), `browser/*` (browser-use, browserbase, firecrawl), `video_gen/*` (fal, xai).
- Any user plugin installed into a category namespace (the **recommended** layout matching bundled plugins) will load at runtime but be invisible to `hermes plugins list`.
- Status reporting (`_plugin_status`) only checks the manifest `name` against `plugins.enabled`, not the path-derived key, so even if a user manually adds `web/tinyfish` to `plugins.enabled`, the CLI shows "not enabled" because it compares against the manifest name `web-tinyfish`.

## Steps to Reproduce

```bash
# 1. Create a user plugin in category layout
mkdir -p ~/.hermes/plugins/web/tinyfish
cat > ~/.hermes/plugins/web/tinyfish/plugin.yaml <<'EOF'
name: web-tinyfish
version: 1.0.0
description: "Test plugin"
author: test
kind: backend
provides_web_providers:
  - tinyfish
requires_env: []
EOF

cat > ~/.hermes/plugins/web/tinyfish/__init__.py <<'EOF'
def register(ctx): pass
EOF

# 2. Enable it
hermes plugins enable "web/tinyfish"

# 3. Check the CLI listing — plugin does NOT appear
hermes plugins list
hermes plugins list --user
hermes plugins list --json

# 4. But runtime discovery finds it fine
python3 -c "
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, '.')
from hermes_cli.plugins import PluginManager
pm = PluginManager()
pm.discover_and_load(force=True)
for k, p in pm._plugins.items():
    if 'tinyfish' in k.lower():
        print(f'{k}: enabled={p.enabled}')
"
# → web/tinyfish: enabled=True
```

## Expected Behavior

`hermes plugins list` should discover plugins in nested category directories (up to 2 segments deep), matching the behavior of `PluginManager._scan_directory_level()`. The CLI listing and the runtime scanner should be consistent.

## Actual Behavior

`hermes plugins list` shows only flat plugins (e.g. `disk-cleanup`, `google_meet`) and misses all category-namespaced plugins.

## Root Cause Analysis

The discrepancy exists because two separate code paths implement plugin discovery:

| Component | Function | Recurses into categories? |
|-----------|----------|--------------------------|
| Runtime | `PluginManager._scan_directory_level()` (`hermes_cli/plugins.py:1227`) | Yes (depth <= 2) |
| CLI list | `_discover_all_plugins()` (`hermes_cli/plugins_cmd.py:731`) | No (flat only) |

The runtime scanner correctly handles both layouts:

```
# Flat:     plugins/disk-cleanup/plugin.yaml    → key = "disk-cleanup"
# Category: plugins/web/tavily/plugin.yaml      → key = "web/tavily"
```

The CLI listing only handles flat, causing category plugins to be silently dropped.

Additionally, `_plugin_status()` in `plugins_cmd.py` checks `entry[0]` (the manifest `name`) against the enabled/disabled sets, but for category plugins the config key is path-derived (e.g. `web/tinyfish`) while the manifest name differs (e.g. `web-tinyfish`). This means even manually enabling via config doesn't fix the display.

## Suggested Fix

### 1. Make `_discover_all_plugins()` recurse into category directories

Replace the flat `iterdir()` loop with a recursive `_scan_level()` helper that mirrors `PluginManager._scan_directory_level()` — recurse into directories without `plugin.yaml` up to 2 levels deep, computing the path-derived key with the accumulated prefix.

### 2. Fix `_plugin_status()` to check both name and key

Add the path-derived key to the entry tuple (element 5) and have `_plugin_status()` accept an optional `key` parameter, checking both `name` and `key` against the enabled/disabled sets. This ensures category plugins like `web/tinyfish` show as "enabled" when `web/tinyfish` appears in `plugins.enabled`.

## Proposed Patch

```python
# In _discover_all_plugins():
def _scan_level(path, source, skip_names, prefix, depth):
    """Recursive directory scan matching PluginManager._scan_directory_level."""
    if not path.is_dir():
        return
    for d in sorted(path.iterdir()):
        if not d.is_dir():
            continue
        if depth == 0 and skip_names and d.name in skip_names:
            continue
        info = _read_manifest_info(d, prefix)
        if info is not None:
            name, version, description, key = info
            if key in seen and source == "bundled":
                continue
            src_label = source
            if source == "user" and (d / ".git").exists():
                src_label = "git"
            seen[key] = (name, version, description, src_label, d, key)
            continue
        if depth >= 1:
            continue
        sub_prefix = f"{prefix}/{d.name}" if prefix else d.name
        _scan_level(d, source, skip_names=None, prefix=sub_prefix, depth=depth + 1)

# In _plugin_status():
def _plugin_status(name, enabled, disabled, key=""):
    if name in disabled or (key and key in disabled):
        return "disabled"
    if name in enabled or (key and key in enabled):
        return "enabled"
    return "not enabled"
```

## Scope

This bug affects:
- `hermes plugins list` (table, plain, JSON, `--user`, `--enabled` filters)
- `hermes plugins list --user` (user category plugins invisible)
- `hermes plugins list --enabled` (enabled category plugins invisible)
- Status display for category plugins (shows "not enabled" even when enabled via config)

It does **not** affect:
- `hermes plugins enable/disable` (uses `_plugin_exists` which does iterate all subdirs)
- Runtime plugin loading (`PluginManager._scan_directory_level` already handles categories)
- Gateway/platform adapters (loaded by the runtime scanner, not the CLI listing)

## Related Issues

- #27548 — Platform plugin discovery drops `platforms/` namespace from keys (same root cause family; different aspect)
- #29452 — Dashboard plugin enable/disable routes return 405 for category-namespaced plugins (already closed/fixed)
- #23802 — `hermes plugins enable/list` filters out entry-point-discovered plugins (related gap in same function, different source)

## Environment

- Hermes Agent: v0.13.0+ (commit `e3ae03592`)
- OS: Linux (WSL)
- Python: 3.14.4
- Reproduced with both bundled plugins (`web/*`, `image_gen/*`, `browser/*`, `video_gen/*`) and user-installed plugins (`web/tinyfish`)

items.body:
## Description

When using Xiaomi MiMo (mimo-v2.5) as the provider, tools that return images in their results (e.g., `browser_screenshot`, `vision_analyze`) cause the API to return a 400 error:

```
Error code: 400 - {'error': {'code': '400', 'message': 'Param Incorrect', 'param': 'text is not set', 'type': ''}}
```

## Root Cause

The Xiaomi MiMo API has different requirements for different message types:

- **User messages**: Support list-type content with images ✅
- **Tool messages**: Must be string-only, reject list-type content ❌

When Hermes tools return multimodal results (images), they are placed in `role: "tool"` messages with list-type content containing image parts. The Xiaomi API rejects this format.

## Current Behavior

1. Tool returns image content in `role: "tool"` message
2. API receives list-type content in tool message
3. API returns 400 error "text is not set"
4. Recovery mechanism strips images and retries (losing visual information)

## Expected Behavior

Images from tool results should be preserved and visible to the model, either by:
1. Converting tool messages to text-only and attaching images to the next user message
2. Or finding another way to pass images to the model while respecting API constraints

## Affected Providers

This is not specific to Xiaomi. Multiple providers share this limitation:
- Xiaomi MiMo
- DeepSeek
- MiniMax
- Z.AI/GLM
- Kimi/Moonshot
- Alibaba/Qwen

## Suggested Fix

Modify `_tool_result_content_for_active_model` and `_try_strip_image_parts_from_tool_messages` in `run_agent.py` to:

1. For providers that don't support list-type tool content:
   - Extract images from tool messages
   - Convert tool messages to text-only (preserve text descriptions)
   - Store images temporarily
   - Attach images to the next user message

This preserves the visual information while respecting API constraints.

## Reference

- Related to issue #27344 (mentioned in code comments)
- Xiaomi MiMo API documentation: https://platform.xiaomimimo.com/docs/zh-CN/usage-guide/image-understanding

## Environment

- Hermes version: Latest
- Provider: xiaomi
- Model: mimo-v2.5
- Platform: App (GUI)

## Workaround

The current workaround is to use `image_input_mode: text` in config, which routes all images through the auxiliary vision model. However, this loses the ability for the main model to directly process images.

## Description

The Hermes Desktop settings page is opened by the global keyboard shortcut **Ctrl+,** (defined as `nav.settings` with default combo `mod+,` in `apps/desktop/src/lib/keybinds/actions.ts`).

- While the keybind system does support rebinding (via Ctrl+/ panel), users affected by this bug cannot easily discover or access that panel

2. **Add IME awareness:** Detect IME composition state in the keybind listener and suppress `mod+,` during IME active sessions
3. **Surface keybind panel:** Consider showing a prompt or tooltip during first run on Windows+Chinese locale

## Workaround

Press **Ctrl+/** to open the keybind panel, find `nav.settings` under Navigation, and rebind it to a different key (e.g. Ctrl+Shift+,).

items.title: Feature Request: Feishu platform — real-time task status indicator while agent is processing

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
# Feature Request: Feishu platform — real-time task status indicator while agent is processing

**Labels:** `enhancement`, `platform:feishu`, `ux`

---

## Problem

When Hermes Agent runs a long task on the Feishu platform (e.g., `hermes update`, code generation, multi-step tool chains), the user sees **complete silence** for potentially several minutes. The message is sent, the user waits, and then — suddenly — the final reply arrives. There is **zero** feedback during the entire waiting period.

This is a critical UX gap because:

- Users have no way to know if the agent is actively processing, stuck, or has crashed
- On messaging platforms like Feishu, users expect real-time feedback (similar to ChatGPT/Claude web, Doubao, Kimi official bots)
- OpenClaw's Feishu plugin supports [typing indicators](https://docs.openclaw.ai/concepts/typing-indicators) and streaming cards that show "typing..." status and partial results in real time
- If a long operation times out or is interrupted (e.g., user sends another message), the user gets **no notification** — the message just disappears into silence

### Real examples

1. `hermes update` — takes ~2-5 minutes to download, rebuild venv, restart gateway. User sees nothing.
2. Multi-step delegate_task chains — each step may take 30s-2min. Total silent wait can be 3-10 minutes.
3. Browser automation with `browser_navigate` + `browser_click` chains — network-dependent, unpredictable duration.
4. Cron jobs — user schedules a task, has no idea if it's running, failed, or completed.

### What users expect (benchmark: OpenClaw Feishu plugin)

OpenClaw's Feishu plugin already provides:
- **Typing indicators**: A `typingMode` setting (`thinking`, `message`, `instant`) that periodically sends "typing..." status to the chat
- **Streaming cards**: Feishu CardKit supports real-time typewriter effect via `card_id`
- **Status messages**: When a task completes or fails, the user immediately sees the result or error
- **Streaming chunk delivery**: Responses sent incrementally so users see progress

Hermes Agent on Feishu currently does none of this. Users wait in the dark.

---

## Proposed Solution

Add a **task status indicator system** for the Feishu platform that shows:

### 1. "Thinking" / Typing indicator (Phase 1 — minimal)

When the agent starts processing a message, send a brief Feishu message (or use Feishu's typing indicator API if available) that shows "正在处理..." or a similar status. When the final response is ready, this status is either replaced or followed by the actual reply.

- **Feishu API option**: Use `im.message.statistics.update` or simply send a temporary "processing" message that gets replaced with `im.v1.message.patch` when done
- **Config**: `feishu.show_processing_indicator: true/false` with optional timeout (`feishu.processing_timeout_seconds: 60`)
- **Fallback**: If Feishu's message patch API is unavailable (permission issues), send a separate "processing" message followed by the actual reply

### 2. Progressive status updates during multi-step tasks (Phase 2)

For tasks that involve multiple tool calls or steps (e.g., `delegate_task`, multi-step code generation):

- Every N seconds (configurable), if no output has been sent, send a lightweight status update: "正在分析代码..." / "正在执行步骤 2/5..." / "正在等待 API 响应..."
- These can be simple text messages or card updates
- When the final result is ready, all pending status messages are cleaned up (or kept as a timeline)

### 3. Completion/failure notification (Phase 3)

For long-running operations (especially Cron jobs):

- When the task completes: send the final result immediately to the chat where the user initiated it
- When the task fails: send an error notification with a concise error message
- When the task is interrupted: send a "任务已中断" notification

---

## Technical Approach

### Approach A: Temporary status message + patch (Recommended for Phase 1)

```python
# When agent starts processing:
msg = await client.im.v1.message.create(
    receive_id_type="chat_id",
    content=json.dumps({"text": "⏳ 正在处理中，请稍候..."}),
)
msg_id = msg.data.message_id

# When agent finishes:
await client.im.v1.message.patch(
    message_id=msg_id,
    content=json.dumps({"text": actual_final_response}),
)
```

### Approach B: CardKit streaming card (Recommended for Phase 2-3)

Build on top of existing [CardKit streaming work](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/6363, #16084, #17852):

```python
card_id = await create_streaming_card()
# During processing:
await update_card_streaming(card_id, "⏳ 正在分析...")
# On completion:
await stop_card_streaming(card_id, final_card_json)
```

### Approach C: Hybrid (Best overall)

Use Approach A for the simplest "just let me know something is happening" case, and Approach B for users who want the full streaming card experience. Both can coexist behind config flags.

---

## Configuration

```yaml
# ~/.hermes/config.yaml
platforms:
  feishu:
    show_processing_indicator: true       # Show "processing" status while waiting
    processing_timeout_seconds: 60        # Only show if task exceeds this
    show_step_updates: false              # Show intermediate step messages
    step_update_interval_seconds: 30      # Frequency of step updates
    cardkit_streaming_enabled: false      # Enable CardKit streaming (separate from streaming.enabled)
```

---

## Related Issues

- [#14425](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/14425) — Automatic heartbeat/progress notifications for long-running tools (general, not Feishu-specific)
- [#6363](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/6363) — Native streaming with Feishu's CardKit
- [#7675](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/7675) — Feishu card interaction & streaming card support
- [#16084](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/16084) — CardKit streaming instead of `im.v1.message.update`
- [#17852](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/17852) — Feishu Streaming Card project
- [#26236](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/26236) — Streaming cards for Feishu

This issue is specifically about the **minimal viable case**: let the user know "I'm working on it" while they wait, and notify them "done" or "failed" when the task ends. This is a prerequisite for building on top of the streaming card work in the related issues.

---

## Environment

- **Platform**: Feishu / Lark (gateway WebSocket mode)
- **Affected channels**: DM, group chats, shared group chats
- **All Hermes versions**: This gap exists across all current releases
- **Reference implementation**: [OpenClaw Feishu plugin typing indicators](https://docs.openclaw.ai/concepts/typing-indicators)

---

## Why this matters

The #1 complaint from Hermes Agent users on messaging platforms (not just Feishu, but especially Feishu where no streaming exists at all) is **"I sent a message and heard nothing back for 5 minutes, not knowing if it worked."** 

This is a basic UX contract that every modern AI assistant fulfills (ChatGPT shows the typing dots, Claude shows incremental text, Doubao/Kimi show streaming cards). Hermes Agent on Feishu has none of this — users are left in the dark.

Fixing this requires **no changes to the core agent loop** — it's purely a platform adapter enhancement. The agent already knows when it starts and ends processing; the gateway just needs to bridge that knowledge into a Feishu message.

items.title: [Telegram gateway] Voice cache timeout dispatches empty user turn
items.body:
## Summary

Telegram voice messages can become silent data loss when the Bot API/CDN times out before the gateway caches the audio. `_handle_media_message()` logs `Failed to cache voice`, but then falls through to `handle_message(event)` with no `media_urls`, no transcript, and usually empty `event.text`. The agent receives a blank user turn and responds generically instead of telling the user to resend the voice memo.

This is the voice-message variant of the broader cache-failure class in #23045, but the observed failure path is specifically `msg.voice.get_file()` timing out before STT can run.

## Observed evidence

A live Telegram gateway session produced this sequence:

```text
[Telegram] Failed to cache voice: Timed out
telegram.error.TimedOut: Timed out
inbound message: platform=telegram ... msg=''
conversation turn: session=<session-id> ... msg=''
Turn ended: reason=text_response ... response_len=25
```

The persisted session contained only:

```text
user: ""
assistant: "Listening 👂 Send it over."
```

There was no `Cached user voice at ...`, no `audio_*.ogg`, and no `Transcribed audio_*.ogg ...` line for that turn, so STT never got an audio path.

## Root cause

In `gateway/platforms/telegram.py::_handle_media_message()`:

```python
if msg.voice:
    try:
        file_obj = await msg.voice.get_file()
        audio_bytes = await file_obj.download_as_bytearray()
        cached_path = cache_audio_from_bytes(bytes(audio_bytes), ext=".ogg")
        event.media_urls = [cached_path]
        event.media_types = ["audio/ogg"]
    except Exception as e:
        logger.warning("[Telegram] Failed to cache voice: %s", e, exc_info=True)
```

After the exception is swallowed, execution continues to the final `await self.handle_message(event)`. Because `event.media_urls` is empty, `_enrich_message_with_transcription()` never runs.

## Expected behavior

If a Telegram voice/audio download fails:

1. Retry briefly for transient Telegram/CDN timeouts.
2. If retry is exhausted, fail closed: send a user-facing notice such as “I received your voice message, but could not download it from Telegram. Please resend it.”
3. Do not dispatch an empty media event into the agent loop.

## Repro shape

1. Send a Telegram voice message to a Hermes gateway.
2. Simulate `msg.voice.get_file()` or `download_as_bytearray()` raising `telegram.error.TimedOut` / a network timeout.
3. Observe the current gateway logs a warning and still sends an empty `msg=''` turn to the agent.

## Related

- #23045 tracks the same silent-loss shape for Telegram document cache failures.
- This issue is narrower: Telegram voice/audio cache failure before STT.

## Summary

Changing an auxiliary model in the Desktop/dashboard model settings updates the auxiliary task's `provider` and `model`, but leaves any existing `auxiliary.<task>.base_url` untouched. If the task was previously configured for a custom/OpenRouter endpoint and is then switched to a built-in provider such as `ollama-cloud`, Hermes can keep routing the auxiliary request to the stale endpoint and fail with misleading provider/model errors.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent: v0.16.0 (2026.6.5), upstream `3289d4ad`
- Local checkout observed at: `846821d8c` on `main` (`origin/main` was 7 commits ahead at report time)
- UI path: Desktop/dashboard model settings
- Affected slot observed: `auxiliary.compression`

## Reproduction

1. Configure compression as a custom/OpenRouter auxiliary model, leaving a per-task base URL like:
   ```yaml
   auxiliary:
     compression:
       provider: custom
       model: '@preset/gemma4-26-b-compress-cached'
       base_url: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1
   ```
2. In the Desktop app model settings, change the compression auxiliary model to Ollama Cloud:
   ```yaml
   provider: ollama-cloud
   model: gemma4:31b
   ```
3. Run `/compress` in a fresh/affected session.

## Actual behavior

The Desktop/backend change leaves the old `auxiliary.compression.base_url` in place, producing a mixed config like:

```yaml
auxiliary:
  compression:
    provider: ollama-cloud
    model: gemma4:31b
    base_url: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1
```

Compression then fails because the Ollama Cloud model ID is sent to the stale OpenRouter endpoint:

```text
Compression summary failed: Error code: 400 - {'error': {'message': 'gemma4:31b is not a valid model ID', 'code': 400}, ...}
```

The provider/model pair itself is valid when routed normally:

```text
hermes chat -Q --provider ollama-cloud -m gemma4:31b -q 'Reply OK only.'
→ OK
```

Clearing the stale auxiliary base URL fixes it:

```bash
hermes config set auxiliary.compression.base_url ""
```

## Expected behavior

When Desktop/dashboard changes an auxiliary task from `custom` or another base-URL-backed endpoint to a built-in provider, it should clear `auxiliary.<task>.base_url` unless the user explicitly supplied a new valid base URL for that task.

This should mirror main model switching behavior: `_apply_main_model_assignment()` already clears stale `model.base_url` when switching main providers away from `custom`.

## Source evidence

In `hermes_cli/web_server.py`, the main-model path calls `_apply_main_model_assignment()`, which reconciles and clears stale `model.base_url` for non-custom providers.

But the auxiliary path in `set_model_assignment()` only writes:

```python
slot_cfg["provider"] = provider
slot_cfg["model"] = model
aux[slot] = slot_cfg
```

It does not clear or reconcile `slot_cfg["base_url"]`.

The Desktop model settings call also sends only `model`, `provider`, `scope: 'auxiliary'`, and `task`, so the stale base URL stays hidden from the user.

## Impact

- `/compress` can fail after a seemingly valid Desktop model switch.
- Error message points at the new model ID (`gemma4:31b is not a valid model ID`) instead of the real stale endpoint/config drift.
- Likely affects other auxiliary slots too, not just compression: vision, web_extract, skills_hub, approval, mcp, title_generation, curator, etc.

## Suggested fix

Add auxiliary-slot base URL reconciliation in `POST /api/model/set`, similar to `_apply_main_model_assignment()`:

- if provider is `custom` and a non-empty `base_url` is supplied, persist it;
- otherwise clear `slot_cfg["base_url"]` when switching to a built-in provider;
- consider doing the same for auxiliary `context_length` or other provider-specific stale fields if applicable;
- add regression coverage for switching `auxiliary.compression` from `custom` with `base_url` to `ollama-cloud`, verifying `base_url` becomes empty.

## Workaround

Manually clear the affected auxiliary task base URL after switching provider:

```bash
hermes config set auxiliary.compression.base_url ""
```

Then restart the affected CLI/gateway/Desktop session so the new config is picked up.

labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Summary

The dangerous-command approval prompt never renders in the classic CLI (non-TUI) mode. The user sees `⏱ Timeout — denying command` after 60 seconds but never sees the approval panel. This effectively makes the approval system unusable — commands are silently denied without user interaction.

## Environment

- hermes-agent 0.15.2
- RHEL 10 (Linux 6.12.0)
- prompt_toolkit (latest via pip)
- Classic CLI mode (`hermes chat`), not `--tui`
- Provider: custom OpenAI-compatible proxy (localhost bridge)

## Root Cause

`_invalidate()` in `cli.py:3273` has a 250ms throttle:

```python
def _invalidate(self, min_interval: float = 0.25) -> None:
    if getattr(self, "_resize_recovery_pending", False):
        return
    now = time.monotonic()
    if hasattr(self, "_app") and self._app and (now - self._last_invalidate) >= min_interval:
        self._last_invalidate = now
        self._app.invalidate()
```

When `_approval_callback` (cli.py:11290) fires on the tool-execution thread, it sets `self._approval_state` and calls `self._invalidate()`. If any other UI event (spinner frame, output flush, completion) triggered an invalidation within the previous 250ms, the approval's invalidation is **silently dropped**. The `ConditionalContainer` wrapping the approval widget never re-evaluates, so the panel never appears.

The retry loop in `_approval_callback` only calls `_invalidate()` every 5 seconds (line 11335), which is too infrequent — by then the user has no visual indicator that approval is pending (only the prompt icon changes to `⚠`, which is easy to miss).

## Code Path

1. Tool thread → `check_dangerous_command()` → `prompt_dangerous_approval()` → `approval_callback()`
2. `_approval_callback` sets `self._approval_state` (dict with command, choices, response_queue)
3. Calls `self._invalidate()` ← **throttled, silently dropped**
4. Polls `response_queue.get(timeout=1)` in a loop
5. Retry `_invalidate()` only every 5 seconds
6. After 60s → timeout → deny

## Proposed Fix

Bypass the throttle for approval-critical invalidations:

```python
# In _approval_callback, replace:
self._invalidate()

# With:
if hasattr(self, "_app") and self._app:
    self._app.invalidate()
```

`app.invalidate()` is prompt_toolkit's thread-safe redraw method. The throttle exists to prevent terminal flicker on slow connections, but approval is a user-blocking modal — it must render immediately regardless of throttle state.

Optionally, add a terminal bell (`\a`) when the approval panel first appears, as an audible signal.

## Impact

Without this fix, `approvals.mode: manual` is non-functional in classic CLI mode. The approval system fires, waits 60 seconds for a response the user can never give, and denies. Users are forced to use `--yolo` / `mode: off` as a workaround.

## Validation

- Reviewed by two independent LLMs (Granite 3.2 8B, Llama Scout 17B) via MaaS fan-out — both confirmed the throttle as root cause and the direct `app.invalidate()` bypass as the correct fix.
- The existing `_force_full_redraw()` method (cli.py:3282) already bypasses the throttle by calling `app.invalidate()` directly, establishing precedent.

items.body:
## Summary

Hermes Desktop can open a native macOS save/download dialog without an explicit user click when a session message or the Artifacts view contains a direct file download URL such as:

```text
https://hermes-assets.nousresearch.com/Hermes-Setup.dmg
```

This is not the desktop updater downloading the DMG. It is a side effect of the background link-title / artifact metadata path navigating a hidden Electron renderer to a non-HTML URL.

## Why this is the root cause

Current code path:

1. Renderer decides that any non-local `http(s)` URL is title-fetchable:
   - `apps/desktop/src/lib/external-link.tsx`
   - `isTitleFetchable()` returns true for any remote `http:` / `https:` URL.
   - `useLinkTitle()` calls `fetchLinkTitle()` automatically when a link is rendered.

2. Main process title resolver first tries curl and then falls back to a hidden BrowserWindow:
   - `apps/desktop/electron/main.cjs`
   - `fetchLinkTitle()` -> `fetchHtmlTitleWithCurl()` -> `fetchHtmlTitleWithRenderer()`
   - `runRenderTitleJob()` creates `new BrowserWindow({ show: false, ... })`
   - then calls `window.loadURL(rawUrl)`.

3. If `rawUrl` is a direct download/attachment (`.dmg`, `.pkg`, `.exe`, `.zip`, etc.), Chromium/Electron treats the hidden navigation as a download and macOS shows a native save dialog.

4. The Artifacts surface can trigger the same bug without opening the chat message directly:
   - `apps/desktop/src/app/artifacts/index.tsx` collects URLs from recent assistant/tool messages.
   - `PrimaryCell()` calls `useLinkTitle(isLink ? artifact.href : null)` for link artifacts.
   - Therefore opening the Artifacts view/sidebar can render a direct download URL and trigger the same hidden BrowserWindow download path.

This makes the bug look like an auto-update / installer-shell issue because the example URL is `Hermes-Setup.dmg`, but any direct-download URL can reproduce it.

## 100% reproduction

On macOS Desktop:

1. Create or keep a session whose assistant/tool message contains this URL as a visible markdown/raw link:

   ```markdown
   https://hermes-assets.nousresearch.com/Hermes-Setup.dmg
   ```

   A realistic source is an assistant answer like:

   ```markdown
   Direct DMG link: https://hermes-assets.nousresearch.com/Hermes-Setup.dmg
   ```

2. Reopen Hermes Desktop to that session, or open the Artifacts view/sidebar while that session is included in the indexed recent sessions.

3. Wait for link title resolution / artifact indexing.

4. Actual: macOS shows a native save dialog for `Hermes-Setup.dmg`, even though the user did not click the link.

5. Expected: background metadata rendering must never trigger a native download dialog. The link should render with a fallback label. A download should only happen after an explicit user click/open action.

I reproduced this locally with:

- macOS arm64
- Hermes Agent v0.16.0
- Desktop app bundle version 0.15.1
- checkout around `v2026.6.5-114-g210f4e706`

The problematic session contained the URL in message content. Archiving that session stopped the popup, which further confirms the trigger is link/artifact rendering rather than updater state.

## Proposed root fix

Please do not fix this only by blocking `.dmg` URLs. Extension filtering is a useful fast path, but the invariant should be stronger:

> Background metadata/preview code must be side-effect-free and must never navigate to a resource that can initiate a browser download. Downloads should require an explicit user action.

A robust fix could be layered like this:

### 1. Add a resource classifier in the main process

Before any title renderer fallback or webview preview load, classify remote URLs with a side-effect-free HTTP request:

- follow redirects within the existing limit
- use `HEAD` where reliable, or a small-budget `GET` fallback
- reject / classify as download when:
  - `Content-Disposition` contains `attachment`
  - `Content-Type` is not HTML-ish (`text/html`, `application/xhtml+xml`)
  - the first bytes do not look like HTML when the content type is missing or generic
- return a structured result, e.g. `{ kind: 'html' | 'download' | 'image' | 'text' | 'unknown', contentType, disposition, finalUrl }`

### 2. Make `fetchLinkTitle()` HTML-only

`fetchLinkTitle()` should parse titles only for resources classified as HTML.

For downloads / attachments / non-HTML:

- cache an empty title
- return `''`
- let the renderer use existing fallback labels (`urlSlugTitleLabel`, `hostPathLabel`, file name, etc.)

This preserves link rendering and manual downloads while preventing background download dialogs.

### 3. Guard the hidden BrowserWindow fallback

If the renderer fallback remains necessary for JS-rendered pages, it should only run after the classifier says the URL is HTML.

Also add a hard download guard to the isolated title session:

```js
const titleSession = session.fromPartition('hermes:link-titles', { cache: false })
titleSession.on('will-download', event => {
  event.preventDefault()
})
```

Electron documents that `event.preventDefault()` cancels downloads in `session.on('will-download')`, so this is the correct backstop for the background title partition.

### 4. Fix URL preview/artifact behavior separately from explicit opens

For Artifacts / Preview rail:

- direct download artifacts should be displayed as link/file rows, not loaded into a hidden or embedded webview for preview
- if the user clicks the artifact, use the existing explicit open/download path
- if a URL preview target is non-HTML or `Content-Disposition: attachment`, render a small “Open externally / Download” state instead of setting `<webview src=...>`

This preserves functionality: users can still click to download/open artifacts. The app simply stops downloading during passive indexing, title fetching, or preview mounting.

### 5. Tests to add

Suggested coverage:

- renderer unit test: `fetchLinkTitle('https://example.com/file.dmg')` or a classified download URL does not call the bridge and returns `''`.
- main-process unit test: `fetchLinkTitle()` returns `''` for `Content-Disposition: attachment` and for `application/octet-stream`.
- main-process test: `hermes:link-titles` session cancels `will-download`.
- Artifacts test: a direct download artifact renders a stable fallback label and does not trigger title fetching.
- Preview test: a non-HTML/attachment URL target renders an external-open/download state rather than mounting a webview to that URL.

## Why this matters

This is surprising and user-hostile because simply opening a chat, reopening the app, or opening the Artifacts sidebar can trigger an OS save dialog. It also makes the issue hard to diagnose because users naturally suspect the updater or installer. The underlying bug is more general: passive rendering code is performing navigations with download side effects.

items.title: [Bug] gateway status falsely reports outdated service on older systemd versions that ignore RestartMaxDelaySec / RestartSteps

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Bug

On older systemd versions, Hermes can keep reporting the gateway user service as outdated even right after it refreshes the unit successfully.

I hit this on my VPS with:
- Ubuntu kernel `5.15.0-106-generic`
- `systemd 249 (249.11-0ubuntu3.9)`

The installed unit logs:
- `Unknown key name 'RestartMaxDelaySec'`
- `Unknown key name 'RestartSteps'`

Hermes still generates those directives unconditionally and later compares the installed unit to the generated unit with strict text matching, so the service can be treated as stale forever on hosts that ignore those keys.

## Reproduction

1. Use a Linux host with an older systemd release that does not support `RestartMaxDelaySec` / `RestartSteps` (for example `systemd 249`).
2. Install or refresh the Hermes gateway user service.
3. Inspect the service logs and note the warnings for the unsupported directives.
4. Run `hermes gateway status` or trigger the refresh path again.
5. Hermes continues to treat the unit as outdated even though the effective service definition is otherwise current.

## Expected behavior

Older systemd hosts should degrade cleanly. Unsupported restart backoff directives should not cause a false outdated/stale report. Hermes should either omit those directives on unsupported hosts or treat units that differ only by ignored directives as current.

## Root cause

`generate_systemd_unit(...)` unconditionally emits `RestartMaxDelaySec=300` and `RestartSteps=5`, while `systemd_unit_is_current()` effectively does a raw text comparison after only minimal whitespace normalization. On hosts where systemd ignores those directives, Hermes has no feature-aware generation or semantic stale-check normalization.

## Fix

Detect host systemd capability before emitting `RestartMaxDelaySec` / `RestartSteps`, and normalize those directives out of stale-check comparisons on hosts that do not support them. That keeps newer hosts strict while letting older hosts degrade cleanly.

I'd like to contribute a fix if this approach makes sense.

items.title: Hermes Desktop Artifacts over-indexes path references and displays Unix-second timestamps as Jan 21
items.body:
## Summary

Hermes Desktop's **Artifacts** page appears to over-index ordinary path-like strings from session/tool output and displays artifact dates as **Jan 21** because Unix-second timestamps are passed directly to JavaScript `Date` as if they were milliseconds.

Observed in Hermes Desktop `v0.16.0` on macOS, checkout commit `0524c9b34`.

## Symptoms

On the Artifacts page:

1. The item count can be implausibly high for a fresh install / short usage history.
2. Many entries are ordinary file paths mentioned in tool output, logs, code snippets, or prior session context rather than generated outputs.
3. Entries from recent June 2026 sessions display as `Jan 21, ~6:40 AM`.

## Root cause suspected

### 1. Timestamp unit mismatch

In `apps/desktop/src/app/artifacts/index.tsx`, artifact records use message/session timestamps directly:

```ts
timestamp: message.timestamp || session.last_active || session.started_at || Date.now()
```

Then display formatting does:

```ts
new Date(timestamp)
```

The SQLite session DB stores timestamps as Unix seconds, e.g. `1780732996.860...` for a June 2026 message. JavaScript `Date` expects milliseconds, so this becomes January 1970. The UI only shows month/day/time, yielding `Jan 21`.

A defensive fix would normalize seconds to milliseconds before sorting/displaying, for example:

```ts
function normalizeTimestamp(timestamp: number): number {
  return timestamp < 1_000_000_000_000 ? timestamp * 1000 : timestamp
}
```

### 2. Artifact detection is too broad

`looksLikeArtifact()` treats any absolute path containing a dot as an artifact:

```ts
return value.startsWith('/') && value.includes('.')
```

The collector also scans assistant/tool messages broadly, including parsed JSON tool results and strings whose key path matches broad hints like:

```ts
/(path|file|url|image|artifact|output|download|result|target)/i
```

This means regular paths inside logs, code snippets, search results, tool outputs, or contextual memory can be counted as artifacts even when Hermes did not generate them.

## Expected behavior

- Artifact dates should match the source message/session dates.
- The Artifacts page should preferably show actual generated outputs/attachments, not every path-like string observed in assistant/tool output.
- If path references are intentionally included, the UI should distinguish "referenced paths" from generated artifacts, or require stronger evidence such as explicit tool output fields, file-write/image-generation outputs, `MEDIA:` attachments, or existing local files.

## Reproduction outline

1. Have a session where assistant/tool output contains many absolute paths with extensions or dotted filenames.
2. Open Hermes Desktop → Artifacts.
3. Observe many path references listed as artifacts.
4. Observe recent session artifacts dated `Jan 21` instead of the actual recent date.

## Privacy note

This report is intentionally sanitized; the observed path examples were local/private and are omitted.

## Symptoms

After a background process completes with `notify_on_complete=true`, the injected notification triggers a new agent processing turn. Under Telegram flood control conditions, the typing indicator persists indefinitely — only cleared by gateway restart.

Observed: typing shown from 14:13 to 18:15+ (4+ hours), ended only after `hermes gateway restart`.

## Evidence

**Gateway log timeline:**
```
14:13:19  Process proc_xxx finished — injecting agent notification
17:29:57  Telegram flood control, waiting 21.0s
17:29:59  Flood control on send (attempt 1/3), retrying in 19.0s
18:15:54  User reports typing persists
-- no further flood control entries after 17:30 --
(User confirms typing only cleared after gateway restart)
```

**Code path analysis:**

`base.py:4040-4057` — typing loop starts with `_keep_typing(chat_id, stop_event=interrupt_event)`
`base.py:3081-3116` — loop refreshes typing every 2s, checks `stop_event`
`base.py:4481` — `finally` block cancels typing task

The normal cleanup path at line 4481 should cancel typing. But the persistence until restart suggests the typing task outlives the `finally` block under specific conditions.

## Suspected root cause

Flood control during message sending creates a window where:
1. `_keep_typing` continues refreshing typing every 2s
2. `send()` with flood control retry may not reach `finally` promptly
3. If `send()` hangs/stalls permanently under extreme flood control, the async task never unwinds to `finally`

The `_keep_typing` loop runs on the same event loop as the `send()` retry — a stalled send blocks everything.

## Reproduction

1. Have a background terminal process with `notify_on_complete=true`
2. Wait for it to complete while Telegram is under flood control
3. Observe typing indicator persists after agent processes notification
4. `hermes gateway restart` clears it

## Environment

- Hermes: git-installed, v0.12.x+
- Platform: Telegram (long polling mode)
- OS: macOS 26.5.1

## [Bug]: Status bar displays fallback model name instead of active primary model

### Description

The TUI status bar shows the **fallback** model name (`mimo-v2.5`) even though the **primary** model (`gpt-5.5` via `openai-codex`) is the one actually serving requests. `hermes status` and the config both correctly report `gpt-5.5`, and responses are generated by gpt-5.5 — only the status bar label is wrong.

This appears to be the opposite direction of [#7385](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/7385) (which reported the status bar stuck on the primary model after fallback was active).

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure `config.yaml` with a primary model and a `fallback_providers` entry:
   ```yaml
   model:
     default: gpt-5.5
     provider: openai-codex
   fallback_providers:
   - api_mode: chat_completions
     base_url: https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1
     model: mimo-v2.5
     provider: opencode-go
   ```
2. Launch the TUI: `hermes --tui`
3. Send a message
4. Observe the status bar at the bottom of the screen

### Expected Behavior

The status bar should display `gpt-5.5` (the active primary model).

### Actual Behavior

The status bar displays `mimo-v2.5` (the fallback model), despite it not being the active model.

### Supporting Evidence

**`hermes status` output** (correctly shows primary):
```
Model:        gpt-5.5
Provider:     OpenAI Codex
OpenAI Codex  ✓ logged in
```

**`config.yaml`** (primary is gpt-5.5):
```yaml
model:
  default: gpt-5.5
  provider: openai-codex
fallback_providers:
- model: mimo-v2.5
  provider: opencode-go
```

**TUI status bar** (incorrectly shows fallback):
`mimo-v2.5 | 20.9K/1M | 2% | 16s | 7s`

**Response content** confirms gpt-5.5 was the actual model used.

### Possible Root Cause

In `cli.py`, `_get_status_bar_snapshot()` may be reading from the fallback provider config instead of `agent.model` / the active session model. The status bar rendering could be picking up the first entry from `fallback_providers` rather than the resolved active model. May also be related to session caching (see #40725).

### Environment

- **OS:** Windows 10
- **Shell:** git-bash (MSYS)
- **Hermes version:** latest (as of 2026-06-07)
- **Primary model:** gpt-5.5 (openai-codex)
- **Fallback model:** mimo-v2.5 (opencode-go)
- **TUI launch:** `hermes --tui`

### Related Issues

- #7385 — opposite direction (status bar stuck on primary when fallback is active)
- #40725 — status bar not refreshing on session switch (cosmetic, similar area)
- #4568 — status bar wrong model during smart routing

items.title: [Bug]: Windows Desktop self-update rebuild fails because running Hermes.exe locks release/win-unpacked files
items.body:
## Summary

On Windows Desktop, the in-app self-update handoff can still rebuild while the running Hermes Desktop process tree is holding files inside `apps/desktop/release/win-unpacked`. The update applies the git update, but the Desktop GUI rebuild fails because Electron/app-builder cannot clean the existing unpacked app directory.

This is related to the broader Windows lock issues in #37731 and #38789, but this report is specifically about the Desktop executable/process tree locking the **GUI release directory** (`release/win-unpacked`), not only the venv or `.pyd` native modules.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11 / Windows_NT 10.0.26200
- Hermes Desktop: v0.16.0 (2026.6.5)
- Python: 3.11.15
- Install path: `C:\Users\katan\AppData\Local\hermes\hermes-agent`
- Observed upstream commits during the failure sequence: `136dae779`, then repaired to `9e631095`
- Interface: Hermes Desktop app, using the staged `hermes-setup.exe --update --branch main` flow

## What happened

1. Triggered Desktop update from the app.
2. The Desktop handed off to the staged updater and logged:

```text
[updates] restart: Handing off to the Hermes updater…
[updates] venv shim unlocked; safe to proceed
[updates] launched updater: C:\Users\katan\AppData\Local\hermes\hermes-setup.exe --update --branch main; exiting desktop to release venv shim
```

3. The update fetched/applied the new source commit and started rebuilding the Desktop GUI.
4. The rebuild failed because the existing unpacked Desktop app directory could not be cleaned:

```text
[before-pack] could not clean C:\Users\katan\AppData\Local\hermes\hermes-agent\apps\desktop\release\win-unpacked
(EPERM, Permission denied: \\?\C:\Users\katan\AppData\Local\hermes\hermes-agent\apps\desktop\release\win-unpacked); continuing

⨯ remove C:\Users\katan\AppData\Local\hermes\hermes-agent\apps\desktop\release\win-unpacked\d3dcompiler_47.dll: Access is denied.

C:\Users\katan\AppData\Local\hermes\hermes-agent\node_modules\app-builder-bin\win\x64\app-builder.exe process failed ERR_ELECTRON_BUILDER_CANNOT_EXECUTE
```

5. A follow-up retry/repair then failed earlier in bootstrap because the backend had relaunched and was holding the venv Python executable:

```text
項目 C:\Users\katan\AppData\Local\hermes\hermes-agent\venv\Scripts\python.exe を削除できません: パス 'python.exe' へのアクセスが拒否されました。
```

## Locking processes observed

Immediately before manual repair, these Hermes processes were still running and using files under the install root:

```text
Hermes.exe
Hermes.exe --type=gpu-process ...
Hermes.exe --type=utility ...
Hermes.exe --type=renderer ... --app-path=...\release\win-unpacked\resources\app.asar
python.exe -m hermes_cli.main dashboard --no-open --host 127.0.0.1 --port 9120
```

After force-stopping only Hermes-local processes, both lock probes succeeded:

```text
UNLOCKED ...\venv\Scripts\python.exe
UNLOCKED ...\apps\desktop\release\win-unpacked\d3dcompiler_47.dll
```

Then the same `scripts\install.ps1 -Branch main -NonInteractive -IncludeDesktop` flow completed successfully.

## Expected behavior

The Windows Desktop update path should not attempt to clean/rebuild `release/win-unpacked` until all Hermes Desktop processes that loaded files from that directory have fully exited.

At minimum, the staged updater should detect and wait for/stop:

- `Hermes.exe` main process
- Electron child processes (`gpu-process`, `renderer`, `utility`)
- Desktop-spawned backend `venv\Scripts\python.exe -m hermes_cli.main dashboard ...`
- Any stale `hermes-setup.exe`/update subprocess from a previous attempt

## Suggested fixes

- Use Windows Restart Manager API or an equivalent lock probe before deleting/rebuilding `apps/desktop/release/win-unpacked`.
- Have the staged updater wait for the full Hermes Desktop process tree to exit, not just the venv shim/backend.
- Do not immediately re-enter bootstrap/update while the freshly relaunched backend is running and locking `venv\Scripts\python.exe`.
- If a lock remains, surface the locking process in the UI instead of showing a generic install failure.
- Consider a separate external broker/update directory so the updater can build into a clean temp path and atomically swap after all locks are released.

## Workaround used

```powershell
# Stop only Hermes-local processes first
Get-CimInstance Win32_Process |
  Where-Object {
    $_.ExecutablePath -like 'C:\Users\katan\AppData\Local\hermes\*' -or
    $_.CommandLine -like '*C:\Users\katan\AppData\Local\hermes\hermes-agent*' -or
    $_.CommandLine -like '*hermes-setup*' -or
    $_.Name -like '*Hermes*'
  } |
  ForEach-Object { Stop-Process -Id $_.ProcessId -Force }

# Then repair/build while Hermes Desktop is not running
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass `
  -File C:\Users\katan\AppData\Local\hermes\hermes-agent\scripts\install.ps1 `
  -Branch main -NonInteractive -IncludeDesktop
```

I then restored the npm-touched `package-lock.json` and repacked once from a clean tree so `install-stamp.json` ended with `dirty: false`.

## Related

- #37731 — Windows installer fails with Access denied while app/leaked child processes hold venv files
- #38789 — Gateway/Dashboard lock native `.pyd` dependencies during update
