items.body:
## Bug Description In Hermes Desktop, the right-rail file preview pane (both Markdown rendered view and source view) does not allow native text selection. Users cannot drag-select text inside the preview to copy it — clicks/drags do nothing visible, and `document.getSelection()` stays empty over those regions. This blocks a common workflow: opening a file in the preview, selecting an excerpt, and pasting it into the chat composer or another app. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Launch Hermes Desktop. 2. Open the right sidebar's file browser, click any text file (e.g. a `.md` or `.py`) so it shows in the right-rail preview. 3. Try to drag-select a paragraph in the rendered Markdown view (or switch to "Source" and try in the Shiki-highlighted source). ## Expected Behavior Text in the preview body is selectable like any other content area. Cmd+C copies it. ## Actual Behavior Selection never starts. The cursor doesn't even change to an I-beam. Nothing is copied. ## Affected Component Other (Desktop / Electron renderer) ## Messaging Platform N/A (Desktop only) ## Debug Report Cannot share `hermes debug share` output — logs contain confidential conversation content. Happy to share sanitized excerpts privately on request. ## Operating System macOS 26.5 (Apple Silicon, arm64) ## Python Version 3.11.x ## Hermes Version Built from `main` (verified at commit corresponding to current `apps/desktop/src/styles.css` lines 394–406 and 641–650). ## Additional Logs / Traceback N/A — pure CSS/markup interaction issue. ## Root Cause Analysis `apps/desktop/src/styles.css` sets `user-select: none` on `body` (lines 403–404) as a desktop-app baseline: ```css body { ... -webkit-user-select: none; user-select: none; ... } ``` It then re-enables selection for an explicit allowlist (lines 641–650): ```css input, textarea, [contenteditable]:not([contenteditable='false']), [data-slot='aui_user-message-root'], [data-slot='aui_assistant-message-content'], [data-selectable-text='true'], [data-selectable-text='true'] * { -webkit-user-select: text; user-select: text; } ``` The right-rail file preview components in `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/right-rail/preview-file.tsx` (`MarkdownPreview` and `SourceView`) match none of those selectors, so the body-level `user-select: none` wins and the rendered preview body becomes unselectable. ```tsx // apps/desktop/src/app/chat/right-rail/preview-file.tsx — MarkdownPreview
{text}
// SourceView (Shiki-highlighted body container)
... {text}
``` ## Proposed Fix Opt these two preview body containers into the existing `data-selectable-text` allowlist — minimal change, no new CSS: ```diff --- a/apps/desktop/src/app/chat/right-rail/preview-file.tsx +++ b/apps/desktop/src/app/chat/right-rail/preview-file.tsx @@ function MarkdownPreview -
+
{text}
@@ function SourceView -
+
``` The line-number gutter intentionally keeps `select-none` (it's a click-target for line drag/select), so this only affects the actual content body. ## Are you willing to submit a PR for this? Cannot push to external forks from my current environment (Amazon Code Defender requires `git-defender --request-repo --reason 3` approval). The patch above is verified locally — feel free to apply it directly, or I can submit once internal approval is granted. ## Verified locally macOS 26.5 / Apple Silicon. Built `apps/desktop` from `local/patches` on top of current `main` and re-packed `app.asar`. After the patch, drag-selection works in both the rendered Markdown preview and the source (Shiki) view; line-number gutter selection behavior is unchanged.

items.title: [Feature]: Unified plugin route selector for per-turn provider/model override (main, delegate, auxiliary)

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: needs-decision
labels.description: Awaiting maintainer decision before any implementation

labels.name: sweeper:not-planned
labels.description: Sweeper: closed per standing maintainer policy (design direction)

items.body:
### Problem or Use Case

Hermes has no **single, stable, plugin-accessible hook** that can override `provider` and `model` for every LLM call site. Routing logic is fragmented across config, heuristics, and failure-recovery paths:

- **Main chat (CLI/gateway):** Model is resolved from `config.yaml`, session `/model` overrides, and optional built-in routing (e.g. `smart_model_routing`). There is no documented plugin API to replace that resolution before agent creation.
- **Auxiliary tasks** (compression, vision, title generation, kanban decompose/specify, approval, etc.): Routed through `agent/auxiliary_client.py` → `_resolve_task_provider_model()` → `call_llm()`, which reads `auxiliary.<task>.*` config or follows `provider: auto` back to the live main model via `set_runtime_main()`. Plugins cannot intercept this path.
- **Delegate/subagents:** Built directly in `tools/delegate_tool.py` with delegation config or parent model; no shared routing hook.
- **Other entry points** (`hermes_cli/oneshot.py`, TUI gateway, API server, cron, background tasks, kanban workers) each resolve model/runtime independently or skip any routing hook entirely.

Existing plugin hooks do not solve this:

| Mechanism | Can change model? | Coverage |
|-----------|-------------------|----------|
| `pre_llm_call` | No — only `{"context": "..."}` injection | Main agent turn, after agent init |
| `pre_api_request` / `post_api_request` | No — observer/tracing payloads | Main agent API loop only |
| `register_middleware("llm_request", …)` | Designed to, but **not wired** into agent or `call_llm()` | None today |
| `smart_model_routing` | Built-in only, not extensible | Main turns, heuristic |
| `fallback_providers` / `try_activate_fallback()` | Reactive failover on errors | Main agent failure recovery |

**Who needs this:** Plugin authors building alternative routing (cost/latency optimization, health-aware selection, profile/task-aware policies, external router integration, adaptive/dynamic model selection) should be able to do so without having to patch core components.

**Concrete pain:** I'm trying to implement a model selection / routing plugin. There is no pre_llm hook that can change the model before turn. Implementing one is very difficult, since model selection happens very differently in different paths: aux, fallback, delegate, default, kanban worker, vision, etc. - and core code needs to be modified in multiple places.


### Proposed Solution

Introduce a **canonical, first-class plugin route selector** — a single resolution function invoked at every model-selection decision point, before credentials are bound and before fallback chains are consulted.

### 1. Plugin API

Add to `PluginContext` (in `hermes_cli/plugins.py`):

```python
def register_route_selector(self, fn: Callable) -> None:
    """Register the per-call model routing callback.

    fn(context: RouteContext) -> RouteResult | None

    Return None to fall through to Hermes defaults (config, smart routing, auto).
    Return a dict to override the effective route for this call.
    Only one route selector per process (second registration warns and is ignored).
    """
```

**`RouteContext`** (suggested fields):

```text
call_kind:     "main_turn" | "auxiliary" | "delegate" | "plugin_llm" | ...
task_id:       str          # e.g. "default", "delegate", "compression", "kanban_decomposer"
profile_id:    str          # active Hermes profile name
user_message:  str          # when available (main turns); may be "" for aux-only calls
primary:       dict         # resolved provider/model/base_url/api_mode before override
platform:      str          # "cli", "telegram", "tui", "api", "kanban", ...
session_id:    str
is_delegate:   bool
extra:         dict         # forward-compatible bag
```

**`RouteResult`** (return value):

```text
model:         str            # required when overriding
provider:      str            # optional; default: keep primary.provider
base_url:      str            # optional; re-resolve credentials when provider changes
api_key:       str            # optional
api_mode:      str            # optional
extra_params:  dict           # optional; merged into request_overrides (reasoning, temperature, etc.)
skip_fallback: bool           # default True when plugin returns a route
```

When a plugin returns a route, that route is **authoritative for that call/turn**: Hermes should not apply `fallback_providers`, auxiliary `fallback_chain`, or `try_activate_fallback()` unless the plugin explicitly returns `None` (fall-through) or sets `skip_fallback: false`.

### 2. Single core resolver

Add `hermes_cli/route_resolution.py` (name flexible):

```python
def resolve_effective_route(context: RouteContext) -> ResolvedRoute:
    """Central model/provider resolution for all Hermes LLM call sites.

    Order:
      1. Plugin route selector (if registered and returns a route)
      2. Built-in per-call-kind defaults (config, session override, smart_model_routing)
      3. Never auto-apply fallback_providers here — fallback remains error-time only
         unless the caller explicitly opts in after a failed API call.
    """
```

All call sites should funnel through this function (or a thin wrapper) instead of duplicating resolution logic.

### 3. Mandatory call-site integration

Invoke `resolve_effective_route()` at minimum from:

| Call site | File(s) | `call_kind` / `task_id` |
|-----------|---------|-------------------------|
| CLI main turn | `cli.py` → `_resolve_turn_agent_config()` | `main_turn` / `default` |
| Gateway main turn | `gateway/run.py` → `_resolve_turn_agent_config()` | `main_turn` / `default` |
| Gateway background/cron | `gateway/run.py` (background agent creation) | `main_turn` |
| Auxiliary LLM calls | `agent/auxiliary_client.py` → `call_llm()` / `_resolve_task_provider_model()` | `auxiliary` / `<task>` |
| Delegate children | `tools/delegate_tool.py` → `_build_child_agent()` | `delegate` / `delegate` |
| Plugin LLM facade | `agent/plugin_llm.py` | `plugin_llm` |
| Oneshot / TUI / API server | `hermes_cli/oneshot.py`, `tui_gateway/server.py`, API server adapter | respective `platform` |

Kanban workers and any code path that calls `call_llm()` or constructs `AIAgent` should inherit routing automatically once `call_llm()` and agent-creation paths are covered.

### 4. Credential re-resolution

When the route selector changes `provider` (or `base_url`), Hermes must re-resolve credentials via `resolve_runtime_provider()` for the **target** provider before building the client. Today, partial implementations only swap `runtime["provider"]` while keeping the session's `api_key`/`base_url`, which breaks cross-provider routing.

### 5. Fallback behavior contract

Document and enforce:

- **Proactive selection** (route selector returns a route): no `fallback_providers` / auxiliary fallback chain for that call. If the selected model fails, normal error handling applies; the plugin may observe failures via `api_request_error` / `post_api_request` and adjust future selections.
- **Fall-through** (route selector returns `None`): existing Hermes behavior unchanged, including error-time `try_activate_fallback()` for the main agent.
- Route selector overrides should **not** be silently undone by `smart_model_routing` heuristics when a plugin route is active (see #8462 for the analogous session-override bug).

### 6. Tests and docs

- Unit tests: route selector override, fall-through, cross-provider credential resolution, auxiliary `call_llm()` interception, delegate child routing, `skip_fallback` semantics.
- Integration test: plugin registers selector → main turn + `call_llm(task="compression")` both use plugin-selected model.
- Document in `website/docs/user-guide/features/plugins.md` and `website/docs/developer-guide/` with a minimal example plugin.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One `register_route_selector()` API, one core resolver, no per-platform patches required by plugin authors.
- [ ] Works for main/default turns, delegate children, and all auxiliary tasks (including plugin-registered `register_auxiliary_task` entries).
- [ ] Works across CLI, gateway (all platforms), TUI, API server, cron/background, and kanban-driven auxiliary calls.
- [ ] Plugin-selected routes bypass proactive fallback chain selection; error-time fallback policy is documented.
- [ ] Returning `None` preserves today's default behavior (backward compatible).
- [ ] Exceptions in the callback are caught and logged; Hermes falls through (fail-open, same as other plugin hooks).


### Alternatives Considered

1. **Extend `pre_llm_call` to return `{"model": ..., "provider": ...}`**  
   Fires after agent init; requires mid-turn `switch_model()` and invalidates prompt cache. Does not cover auxiliary `call_llm()` or delegate child creation. Rejected as primary mechanism.

2. **Wire `register_middleware("llm_request", …)` only**  
   Infrastructure exists (`hermes_cli/middleware.py`, `register_middleware`) but is not invoked from the agent loop or `auxiliary_client.py`. Could work for API-payload rewriting but is lower-level, harder to reason about, and still needs wiring at every outbound call site. Better as a complement for parameter rewriting, not as the primary routing contract.

3. **`smart_model_routing` / config-only `model_routing:` blocks**  
   Built-in, not extensible by third-party plugins without core changes. Related open issues (#30652, #4461, #26027, #1572) describe product features, not a plugin attachment point.

4. **Agent-callable `model_switch` tool (#16525)**  
   Useful for agent-initiated escalation, but not automatic per-call routing and does not cover auxiliary/delegate paths without the agent explicitly calling the tool.

5. **Per-request API header override (#16216)**  
   Solves external router → API server only; does not generalize to auxiliary, delegate, or CLI.

6. **Continue patching `cli.py` + `gateway/run.py`**  
   Works short-term (community patches exist) but does not scale across Hermes releases or call-site matrix.

**Recommended approach:** Resolve route **before client/agent creation**, centralized in one module, invoked from `call_llm()` and agent-creation paths. Optionally layer `llm_request` middleware later for fine-grained request-body tweaks.


### Feature Type

Other

### Scope

Large (new module or significant refactor)

### Contribution

- [x] I'd like to implement this myself and submit a PR

items.title: feat: add env-var/config toggle for Telegram pending-updates catch-up on startup

labels.name: sweeper:not-planned
labels.description: Sweeper: closed per standing maintainer policy (design direction)

items.body:
**Problem**

When Hermes Gateway restarts after being offline (e.g. WSL downtime, machine sleep, process restart), messages sent during the outage are silently dropped. The Telegram adapter hardcodes `drop_pending_updates=True` in both webhook and polling startup paths, which tells Telegram to discard all queued updates.

**Proposed Solution**

Add an env var (e.g. `TELEGRAM_CATCHUP_ON_STARTUP`) that controls the `drop_pending_updates` parameter passed to `start_polling()` / `start_webhook()` in `gateway/platforms/telegram.py`:

- `TELEGRAM_CATCHUP_ON_STARTUP=true` → `drop_pending_updates=False` (processes missed messages)
- `TELEGRAM_CATCHUP_ON_STARTUP=false` → `drop_pending_updates=True` (current behavior, discards)
- Default to `false` to preserve existing safe behavior (prevent flood after long outages)

**Affected Lines**

`gateway/platforms/telegram.py`:
- Line ~1686: `drop_pending_updates=True` in webhook `start_webhook()` call
- Line ~1719: `drop_pending_updates=True` in polling `start_polling()` call

**Acceptance Criteria**

- [ ] Env var `TELEGRAM_CATCHUP_ON_STARTUP` is read on gateway startup
- [ ] When set to `true`, pending updates are fetched and processed instead of dropped
- [ ] Default behavior (env var unset or `false`) matches current behavior
- [ ] Both webhook and polling modes respect the toggle

items.title: Bug: auxiliary title_generation requests /v1/v1/messages (404) when provider base_url ends in /anthropic

labels.name: comp/agent

items.body:
## Bug: title_generation auxiliary produces `/v1/v1/messages` (404) when main agent uses `minimax-m3` built-in provider

### Environment
- Hermes Agent (NousResearch) – latest main
- Model: `MiniMax-M3` via built-in provider `minimax-m3`
- Base URL configured: `https://api.minimax.io/anthropic`
- Profile: any (reproduced on `default` and `figlia` profiles)
- Claude Code 1.16.0 bin

### Summary
After every chat turn, the gateway warns:
`⚠ Auxiliary title generation failed: HTTP 404: 404 page not found` (or `Connection error`)

Investigation shows the auxiliary client requests `POST https://api.minimax.io/v1/v1/messages` — a double `/v1/v1/` path. The main chat call uses the same provider successfully via `/anthropic/v1/messages`.

### Reproduction
1. Configure a profile with provider `minimax-m3` (or any custom provider whose base URL ends in `/anthropic`)
2. Run `hermes --profile <name> chat -q "ping" --verbose`
3. Observe: main chat returns 200 OK on `POST https://api.minimax.io/anthropic/v1/messages`
4. Observe: title_generation aux tries `POST https://api.minimax.io/v1/v1/messages` → 404
5. Or with explicit `base_url: https://api.minimax.io/v1`: aux gets `openai.APIConnectionError`

### Root cause
`agent/auxiliary_client.py:_*maybe_rewrite_anthropic_base_url` rewrites the base URL from `…/anthropic` to `…/v1` (for OpenAI-SDK compatibility). But the same code path then hands the rewritten URL to the Anthropic SDK, which appends `/v1/messages` by default → result: `/v1/v1/messages`.

Tested with `api_mode: chat_completions` configured explicitly — fails with `openai.APIConnectionError: Connection error` from the daemon thread, even though the same OpenAI client + base URL works fine from a standalone Python REPL (no `cli.py` threading). Suspected stale httpx transport pool after main agent streaming closes (cf. issue #23432 about cached-client eviction).

### What I tried (all fail)
- Removing the `title_generation` section from `auxiliary:` config (auto-detect hits the same bug)
- `provider: openai` with `base_url: https://api.minimax.io/v1` and `api_mode: chat_completions`
- Forcing `AUXILIARY_*_API_KEY` env vars to real 125-char values
- Various combinations of explicit `api_mode`, `base_url`, `provider`

### Workarounds for users
None clean. The warning is purely cosmetic — main chat still works. Workarounds:
- Set session title manually with `/title <text>`
- Live with the warning (current state)
- Patch `auxiliary_client.py` locally to skip the rewrite when `api_mode` is explicitly set

### Related issues
- #27877 — Feature: add `enabled` toggle for auxiliary tasks (title_generation, etc.) — would let us disable this entirely
- #23246 — Gateway should keep auto-title generation failures silent (covers the user-visible warning)
- #24029 — Auxiliary tasks silently fall back to paid OpenRouter models
- #6838 — Frequent RemoteProtocolError / Connection drops with MiniMax provider
- #32729 — auxiliary title generation config is hardcoded to 30s and ignores config
- #23432 — referenced in code comments about cached-client eviction after timeout

### Suggested fix
In `auxiliary_client.py:_maybe_rewrite_anthropic_base_url`, skip the rewrite when the explicit `api_mode` is set (e.g. `chat_completions`). The current rewrite assumes "anthropic-style" default, but explicit `api_mode` signals the user already knows the endpoint layout.

Alternative: detect double-`/v1` URLs and trim before passing to SDK.

### Debug logs
```
09:28:27 - agent.auxiliary_client - DEBUG - Auxiliary client: rewrote base URL https://api.minimax.io/anthropic → https://api.minimax.io/v1
09:28:58 - agent.auxiliary_client - INFO - Auxiliary title_generation: using auto (MiniMax-M3) at https://api.minimax.io/v1
09:28:59 - anthropic._base_client - DEBUG - HTTP Response: POST https://api.minimax.io/v1/v1/messages "404 404 Page not found"
```

items.title: Feature Request: Integrate Kanban Board into Desktop App
items.body:
Context:
The Kanban board is a powerful tool for multi-agent workflows, but its separation from the desktop app creates friction for users who rely on it daily. Currently, switching between the chat interface and the Kanban board requires:
- Opening a separate terminal/CLI.
- Manually running commands like hermes kanban list or hermes kanban claim.
- Copying task IDs between apps.
This disrupts focus and slows down workflows that depend on real-time task coordination.

Proposal:
Integrate the Kanban board into the desktop app with one (or both) of these approaches:

Option 1: Collapsible Sidebar (GUI)
- Add a minimal Kanban sidebar to the desktop app (collapsible by default).
- Show:
  - Tasks claimed by the current profile.
  - Task status (⏳ In Progress / ✅ Completed / ❌ Blocked).
  - One-click access to task details (no CLI digging).
- Example UI:
  ![Mockup](https://i.imgur.com/xyz123.png) (https://i.imgur.com/xyz123.png) (Imagine a thin sidebar on the right with task cards.)

Option 2: In-Chat Commands (/kanban)
- Extend slash commands to interact with the Kanban board without leaving the chat:
  - /kanban list – Show tasks in the chat (filterable by status/agent).
  - /kanban claim 123 – Claim a task and start working on it immediately.
  - /kanban update 123 --status blocked --reason "Merge conflict" – Update task status.
  - /kanban tail – Stream live updates (like tail -f for the board).
- Notifications for task updates (e.g., "Task #123 blocked by merge conflict") could appear as system messages in the chat.

Why This Matters:
1. Reduces Context-Switching
   - Users like me (who juggle multiple tasks/agents) can stay in one app instead of Alt+Tabbing between terminals.
2. Preserves Multi-Agent Flexibility
   - The board remains profile-agnostic, but the desktop app could show only the tasks relevant to the current profile.
3. Lowers Barrier to Entry
   - New users won’t need to learn CLI commands to use the Kanban board effectively.

Trade-Offs Considered:
- Footprint: A collapsible sidebar or in-chat commands would add minimal overhead (only loaded when opened).
- Stability: The board’s SQLite backend could run as a lightweight subprocess, isolated from the main chat loop.
- Flexibility: Users who prefer the CLI could still use hermes kanban commands in the terminal.

Alternatives Explored:
- Cron Jobs: Auto-syncing the board with chat (e.g., "Alert me if a task is blocked") helps but doesn’t solve the core issue.
- Tiling Windows: Keeping the board open alongside the desktop app works but is visually cluttered.

- Are there technical blockers (e.g., SQLite sync, multi-profile conflicts) that need addressing first?
- Would a beta flag (e.g., --enable-kanban-sidebar) be a viable first step?

labels.name: sweeper:not-planned
labels.description: Sweeper: closed per standing maintainer policy (design direction)

items.body:
## Problem

When `delegate_task()` spawns a subagent with a model that cannot load (model not found, OOM on resource-constrained hardware, API unreachable), the entire delegation task fails after a timeout with no attempt to retry with an alternative model.

On systems like M1 Mac with 16GB RAM, a delegation model that is technically loadable (e.g. ~12GB) can time out during model loading while a smaller model (e.g. ~7GB) would work fine. Previously this resulted in a hard failure with 0 API calls and no recourse.

## Root Cause

`_run_single_child()` had no fallback logic. When a subagent timed out with 0 API calls, the timeout was returned as-is. The `delegation.fallback_models` config option existed in some configurations but was never read or used by the delegation code path.

## Proposed Fix

PR #41224 adds credential chain fallback logic to `delegate_task()`:

1. `_resolve_delegation_credential_chain()` resolves the configured `delegation.fallback_models` array alongside the primary model
2. `_run_single_child()` checks for 0-API-call timeouts and retries with the next fallback in the chain
3. Recursive retry: the child rebuilds with fallback credentials and re-runs the same goal/context

**Config example:**
```yaml
delegation:
  model: mistral-nemo:12b
  provider: ollama-local
  fallback_models:
    - model: qwen2.5:14b
      provider: ollama-local
```

**Tested locally:** Primary (mistral-small:22b) failed silently → fell through to mistral-nemo:12b → completed successfully.

## Related

- PR #41224: delegation fallback model chain

### Summary

When `/sessions` is sent through a messaging gateway, the command is advertised/recognized as a slash command but is not handled natively by the gateway dispatcher. It falls through to the normal agent turn, where the model decides to call `session_search({})`, and then generates the final human-readable session list.

This makes `/sessions` slower and model-dependent, and it persists an assistant tool-call turn plus a tool result for what appears to be a deterministic slash command.

### Reproduction

1. Run a messaging gateway with session history enabled.
2. Send `/sessions` from a messaging platform chat.
3. Inspect the persisted messages for that turn.

Observed message sequence from a local run:

```text
user      /sessions
assistant tool_calls: session_search({})
tool      session_search returns recent sessions JSON
assistant final text list of recent sessions
```

### Actual behavior

The gateway accepts `/sessions` as a known slash command, but there is no native gateway dispatch branch for `canonical == "sessions"`. The command reaches normal model processing. The model then calls the `session_search` tool and formats the final response.

The `session_search` tool itself is deterministic and does not call the model; the model involvement comes from the command falling through to the agent turn.

### Expected behavior

`/sessions` should be handled directly by the gateway slash-command layer, similar to the CLI implementation:

- Bare `/sessions` or `/sessions list` should list recent sessions directly from the session DB.
- `/sessions <id_or_title>` should delegate to the existing resume flow, matching CLI behavior.
- No model call, assistant tool-call message, or tool-result message should be required for the bare list command.

If native gateway support is not intended, `/sessions` should not be advertised as a gateway-available command.

### Relevant code paths

- `hermes_cli/commands.py`: `CommandDef("sessions", "Browse and resume previous sessions", "Session")` is registered without `cli_only=True`.
- `cli.py`: `_handle_sessions_command()` exists and handles the command directly in the CLI.
- `gateway/run.py`: the gateway dispatcher handles many canonical commands, including `resume`, but has no `canonical == "sessions"` branch.
- `tools/session_search_tool.py`: `session_search()` browse mode returns recent sessions without any model call.

- Source commit inspected locally: `9af54b2f8c0e968156e962935d153a2981e7b360`
- Messaging platform observed: Feishu

items.body:
**Bug Description:**
Running `hermes update` on Windows (native) deletes the `gateway-service/` directory under `%HERMES_HOME%`. The existing Windows Scheduled Task still shows "Ready" status but points to a `.cmd` file that no longer exists. The gateway appears to be fine (status shows Ready) but no process is actually running and Telegram stops responding until the service is manually reinstalled.

**Steps to Reproduce:**
1. Install Hermes on Windows (native, no WSL), configure Telegram gateway, confirm it works
2. Run `hermes update`
3. Check `hermes gateway status` — shows "Ready" but "No gateway process detected"
4. Check `%HERMES_HOME%\gateway-service\` — directory is gone
5. Check the Scheduled Task (SchTasks) — `Task To Run` points to the deleted `Hermes_Gateway.cmd`
6. Gateway remains dead until `hermes gateway install` is re-run

**Expected Behavior:**
Running `hermes update` should either:
- Preserve the `gateway-service/` directory and its scripts, OR
- Automatically reinstall the gateway service after the update completes, OR
- At minimum, warn the user that the gateway service needs to be reinstalled

**Actual Behavior:**
The update silently removes the gateway service files. The user only discovers the issue when they notice Telegram is unresponsive, while `hermes gateway status` misleadingly reports "Ready" because the Scheduled Task still exists.

**Affected Component:** Gateway (Telegram), Setup / Installation

**Operating System:** Windows 10 (native, no WSL)

**Hermes Version:** v0.16.0 (2026.6.5)

**Python Version:** 3.11.15

**Debug Report:**
- Report: https://paste.rs/YUgWH
- agent.log: https://paste.rs/x8A1h
- gateway.log: https://paste.rs/DjJiC
- desktop.log: https://paste.rs/2I4L4

**Root Cause Analysis:**
The `hermes update` process restores/rebuilds the installation directory without preserving the `gateway-service/` subdirectory that was created by `hermes gateway install`. The Windows Scheduled Task (`Hermes_Gateway`) survives the update because it is registered in Windows Task Scheduler, not in the filesystem, so it continues to report "Ready" even though its target executable no longer exists.

**Workaround:**
Running `hermes gateway install` recreates the `gateway-service/` directory and script, and restarts the gateway.

items.title: bug: /model command blocks Discord event loop for 120-150s, causing "application did not respond" and delayed agent starts

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
## Summary

When the `/model` slash command is used on Discord, the gateway's async event loop is blocked for 120–150 seconds by a synchronous HTTP call. This causes two symptoms:

1. **"The application did not respond"** — Discord requires a slash command response within 3 seconds; the blocked loop guarantees a timeout.
2. **2–3 minute delay before agent starts tool calling** — messages sent while the loop is frozen queue up and are not processed until the block clears.

## Root Cause

`_handle_model_command` in `gateway/run.py` calls `list_picker_providers()` and `list_authenticated_providers()` **directly on the event loop** (no `await`, no `asyncio.to_thread`). These functions call down to `_fetch_anthropic_models()` → `urllib.request.urlopen()` (blocking I/O) when the provider model cache is stale.

The cache uses a credential fingerprint that includes the mtime of `~/.claude/.credentials.json`. When the Claude Code OAuth token refreshes (roughly every hour), the mtime changes → cache miss → live network request → **event loop frozen**.

Call chain:
```
_handle_model_command (async, runs on event loop)
  └─ list_picker_providers()             # sync, no to_thread
       └─ list_authenticated_providers()
            └─ cached_provider_model_ids()
                 └─ provider_model_ids()
                      └─ _fetch_anthropic_models()
                           └─ urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=5.0)  # blocks loop
```

From `gateway.error.log`:
```
WARNING discord.gateway: Shard ID None heartbeat blocked for more than 10 seconds.
...
WARNING discord.gateway: Shard ID None heartbeat blocked for more than 150 seconds.
```

## Fix

Wrap both synchronous calls in `asyncio.to_thread()` in `gateway/run.py`:

```python
# Picker path (~line 11165)
import functools
providers = await asyncio.to_thread(
    functools.partial(
        list_picker_providers,
        current_provider=current_provider,
        current_base_url=current_base_url,
        current_model=current_model,
        user_providers=user_provs,
        custom_providers=custom_provs,
        max_models=50,
    )
)

# Text fallback path (~line 11314)
providers = await asyncio.to_thread(
    functools.partial(
        list_authenticated_providers,
        current_provider=current_provider,
        current_base_url=current_base_url,
        current_model=current_model,
        user_providers=user_provs,
        custom_providers=custom_provs,
        max_models=5,
    )
)
```

This lets the event loop remain responsive (Discord heartbeats, incoming messages) while the model list fetch runs in a worker thread.

## Environment

- Platform: macOS Darwin 25.2.0
- Gateway platform: Discord
- Trigger: `/model` slash command when `~/.claude/.credentials.json` mtime has changed since last cache fill (i.e. after OAuth token refresh)

items.title: GPT-5.5 (openai-codex): pre-tool-call preamble text leaks as visible assistant content to chat gateways since v0.16.0
items.body:
### Summary

Since **v0.16.0** (`v2026.6.5`), GPT-5.x models on the **`openai-codex`** provider emit their short pre-tool-call "preamble" text as **standalone, user-visible assistant message items** (content channel). On chat gateways (Telegram in my case) these are delivered to the end user as interim messages — raw, telegraphic English internal-planning text ("Need patch …", "Convert.", "Vision.") — even though the final answer is correctly formatted. On v0.15.1 the same model kept this text in the reasoning channel, so nothing leaked.

### Environment

- Hermes-Agent **v0.16.0** (`v2026.6.5`); regressed vs **v0.15.1** (`v2026.5.29.2`)
- Provider **`openai-codex`** (ChatGPT codex backend), model gpt-5.5
- Gateway: **Telegram**; terminal backend: docker
- `display.show_reasoning: false` (does not gate this — it's content, not reasoning)

### Expected vs. actual

- **Expected:** pre-tool-call model planning stays internal (reasoning channel), as on v0.15.1.
- **Actual:** it is surfaced as visible assistant content and delivered mid-turn to the chat user.

### Evidence

- **Version boundary:** under v0.15.1, gpt-5.5 ran for ~2 days under heavy tool/vision/playwright load with **0** content-leak turns. The first sessions on v0.16.0 leak.
- **Field-level (session store):** leak turns are `role=assistant`, `finish_reason=tool_calls`, **non-empty `content`** but **empty `reasoning_content` / `codex_reasoning_items`**. Clean turns are the inverse (reasoning populated, content empty). So on leak turns the model emits a message item *instead of* a reasoning item.
- **Conditional, not constant:** within a single v0.16.0 session it stayed clean for hours, then started leaking on a long autonomous tool/vision grind — consistent with GPT-5 emitting preambles only situationally, now surfaced by v0.16.0.

### Suspected mechanism

The v0.16.0 backend rework appears to reclassify "intermediate assistant text emitted before a tool call" as standalone message items — same mechanism reported (opposite direction, items *dropped*) in #39558 and #40903 for Desktop. On gateways the delivery path (`_emit_interim_assistant_message` → `interim_assistant_callback`) bypasses `transform_llm_output`, cf. #35264 (proposal) and #27442.

### Impact

Customer-facing chat agents leak raw internal English planning to end users, breaking persona/localization and exposing chain-of-thought-like text.

### Workaround

`display.platforms.<platform>.interim_assistant_messages: false` stops delivery — but also suppresses legitimate interim commentary; it's a blunt mitigation.

### Asks

1. Don't surface pre-tool-call preamble items as default-visible content on gateways (or route them through `transform_llm_output`).
2. A dedicated config switch / transform hook to gate interim/preamble content (cf. #35264).

### Bug Description
The Kanban dispatcher injects `--skills kanban-worker` into every spawned worker, gated by `_kanban_worker_skill_available()` (hermes_cli/kanban_db.py around line 6548). That check uses a recursive `rglob("kanban-worker/SKILL.md")`, which also matches an ARCHIVED copy at `<skills>/.archive/kanban-worker/SKILL.md`. It therefore reports the skill "available" and injects the flag, but the skill loader excludes `.archive/`, so preloading fails at CLI startup with `ValueError: Unknown skill(s): kanban-worker`, aborting the worker before the agent loop runs.

Net effect: any profile that has had `kanban-worker` archived (for example via skill consolidation / skill_manage) cannot run Kanban workers. Every dispatch crashes, and after failure_limit (default 2) consecutive crashes the task is auto-blocked, even though the function docstring says its purpose is to "gate the flag on actual resolvability."

### Steps to Reproduce
1. On a worker-capable profile, archive the bundled kanban-worker skill (move skills/devops/kanban-worker/ into skills/.archive/kanban-worker/).
2. Dispatch any Kanban task to that profile.
3. The worker spawns with `--skills kanban-worker` and exits non-zero with `Error: Unknown skill(s): kanban-worker`.
4. After 2 crashes the dispatcher marks the task gave_up / blocked.

### Expected
_kanban_worker_skill_available() should mirror the loader's resolution, excluding `.archive/` (and other disabled-skill locations), so it returns False when kanban-worker is not actually loadable. The dispatcher then gracefully skips the flag (the lifecycle contract is still injected via KANBAN_GUIDANCE) instead of injecting a flag that crashes the worker.

### Environment
Hermes Agent v0.16.0; also unchanged on current main (fa8fd513e, 2026-06-07): the availability-check / `.archive` handling is untouched in the 129 commits since v0.16.0. Repro is filesystem-level and backend-independent.

items.title: [Bug]: Kanban worker resolves relative file paths against TERMINAL_CWD (gateway home), not the assigned HERMES_KANBAN_WORKSPACE
items.body:
### Bug Description
A Kanban worker is launched with its process cwd set to the task workspace (subprocess cwd=workspace) and HERMES_KANBAN_WORKSPACE set, but file-tool writes that use a RELATIVE path do not land in the workspace. They land under the gateway user's home directory.

Root cause is the file tool's base-directory resolver (tools/file_tools.py, `_resolve_base_dir`, around line 120), which selects, in order: the live terminal cwd, then `$TERMINAL_CWD`, then the process cwd. The Kanban worker env builder (hermes_cli/kanban_db.py, around line 6653) sets HERMES_KANBAN_WORKSPACE and the worker process cwd, but does NOT set TERMINAL_CWD. The worker therefore inherits TERMINAL_CWD from the gateway, where a config `terminal.cwd` of `.` (or `auto`/`cwd`/unset) is rewritten to the home directory (gateway/run.py, around line 1126). So `_resolve_base_dir` returns the gateway home, and a relative write like `wiki/deliverables/research/x.md` resolves to `~/wiki/deliverables/research/x.md` instead of `<workspace>/wiki/deliverables/research/x.md`.

Net effect: a worker that writes a relative artifact path silently writes outside its workspace into the gateway user's home; the workspace receives nothing. With a profile-scoped write guard this presents as a guard/tooling mismatch: relative paths "succeed" to the wrong place while absolute paths are denied.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Use a profile with `terminal.cwd: "."` (the common default), so the gateway exports TERMINAL_CWD=<home>.
2. Create a Kanban task with an explicit workspace (workspace_kind=dir, workspace_path=<dir>) assigned to that profile.
3. In the worker, call write_file with a RELATIVE path, e.g. `report.md`.
4. The file is created at `<home>/report.md`, not `<workspace>/report.md`, even though HERMES_KANBAN_WORKSPACE and the process cwd are the workspace.

### Expected
A Kanban worker's relative file writes should resolve against its assigned workspace (= its process cwd = HERMES_KANBAN_WORKSPACE). Fix options:
- Set `TERMINAL_CWD = workspace` in the worker env builder (hermes_cli/kanban_db.py), or
- Have `_resolve_base_dir` prefer HERMES_KANBAN_WORKSPACE when running inside a Kanban worker.

### Environment
Hermes Agent v0.16.0; code paths unchanged on current main (fa8fd513e, 2026-06-07). Local terminal backend (not codex_app_server). Distinct from #27941 (codex sandbox writable-root / read-only-FS); this is file-tool base-dir selection, backend-independent.

items.title: Feature: Add stall detector — stop when N consecutive tool calls produce no progress

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Problem

The agent loop has `max_iterations` and budget limits, but no mechanism to detect when the agent is **spinning its wheels** — making consecutive tool calls that produce the same or equivalent results without making progress toward the task goal.

Real-world examples observed:

1. **Repeated patch attempts**: agent tries to patch a file, gets "could not find a match", re-reads the file, tries the same old_string again with slightly different whitespace — repeat 5-8 times
2. **Read-check loop**: agent reads a file, finds an issue, reads another file, goes back to the first file, re-reads it, re-confirms the same issue — no forward progress
3. **Same-error retry cycle**: agent calls an API, gets a transient error, retries with identical parameters 3-4 times

This was highlighted in the Harness Engineering article (WeChat, April 2026) which identifies **"no progress — repeating the same action across consecutive rounds"** as one of the 4 essential stop conditions that every agent harness must implement.

A good harness should detect when the agent is "repeating the same kind of action across consecutive rounds" and stop before burning through the entire iteration budget.

## Proposed Solution

Add a **stall detector** that tracks the action signature of each tool call (tool name + normalized arguments hash) and triggers an interrupt when:

- N (configurable, default 3) consecutive tool calls have the same action signature (identical tool name + similar arguments)
- OR M (configurable, default 5) out of the last W (window, default 7) calls share the same action signature with no intermediate user-facing output

On stall detection, the agent should:
1. Log a stall warning
2. Return a structured message to the LLM: "You have repeated the same action X times. Summarize what you have learned and propose a new approach, or ask the user for guidance."
3. Increment a stall counter — if stall count exceeds max_stalls (configurable, default 2), hard-stop with a "stalled" exit reason

## Implementation Sketch

```python
class StallDetector:
    def __init__(self, max_consecutive_stall=3, max_stall_bursts=2, window=7):
        self.tool_history: list[ToolCallSignature] = []
        self.stall_count = 0

    def record(self, tool_name: str, args: dict) -> bool:
        sig = self._make_signature(tool_name, args)
        self.tool_history.append(sig)
        return self._detect()

    def _make_signature(self, name: str, args: dict) -> str:
        # Normalize: strip timestamps, session IDs, nonces
        normalized = {k: v for k, v in args.items()
                      if k not in ("session_id", "timestamp", "nonce")}
        return f"{name}:{hash(json.dumps(normalized, sort_keys=True))}"

    def _detect(self) -> bool:
        # Consecutive check: last N signatures identical?
        if len(self.tool_history) >= self.max_consecutive:
            recent = self.tool_history[-self.max_consecutive:]
            if len(set(recent)) == 1:
                return True
        # Window check: M out of last W identical?
        if len(self.tool_history) >= self.window:
            window = self.tool_history[-self.window:]
            most_common = max(set(window), key=window.count)
            if window.count(most_common) >= 5:
                return True
        return False
```

## Integration Points

- `run_agent.py` `run_conversation()` — add `StallDetector` check in the main loop alongside `_budget_grace_call` and `_interrupt_requested`
- `cli.py` — surface stall events in interactive mode
- `hermes_constants.py` — add config defaults for `max_consecutive_stall` and `max_stall_bursts`

## Alternatives Considered

1. **Simple action-counter per tool** — too coarse, does not detect cross-tool stalls (read -> read -> read cycle)
2. **LLM self-diagnosis** — "are you making progress?" injected into system prompt — unreliable, LLM struggles to self-assess
3. **Output diffing** — compare assistant outputs between rounds — expensive and language-model-dependent

## References

- The "4 stop conditions" pattern from "10 sentences on Harness Engineering" (April 2026)
- Existing `_budget_grace_call` mechanism in `run_conversation()` — stall detector is a complementary signal
- Similar concept: timeout-based circuit breakers in distributed systems

items.title: Feature: Classify tool errors by type for smarter recovery (model vs tool vs environment vs input)

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Problem

When a tool call fails in the agent loop, the current error handling treats all failures uniformly — log the error, retry, or present the error message back to the LLM. This is suboptimal because different error types need fundamentally different recovery strategies:

| Error Type | Example | Correct Response | Current Behavior |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Model error** (bad assumption) | patch old_string doesn't exist; reading wrong file | Tell LLM its assumption was wrong, suggest re-reading | Retry same operation -> stall |
| **Tool error** (transient) | Network timeout, API rate limit | Wait + retry with backoff | Immediate retry -> same failure |
| **Environment error** (hard failure) | File not found, permission denied | Stop, report to user, don't retry | Retry -> same failure * N |
| **Missing input** (needs user) | Ambiguous parameter, missing credential | Ask user, don't retry | Confused retry -> stall |

Without error type classification, the agent burns iterations retrying hopeless operations. The "Harness Engineering" framework identifies this as a critical harness capability: "on failure, identify the failure type (model error, tool error, environment error, missing input) -> write to State (reason, attempts made, next suggestion) -> choose recovery action."

## Proposed Solution

Add lightweight error classification to the tool call result processing in the agent loop.

### Phase 1: Error Classifier

A simple heuristic classifier that tags each tool error with a type:

```python
class ErrorClassifier:
    TOOL_ERROR_PATTERNS = [
        r"timeout", r"rate limit", r"429", r"503",
        r"connection refused", r"temporary",
    ]
    ENV_ERROR_PATTERNS = [
        r"permission denied", r"no such file", r"not found",
        r"ENOENT", r"EACCES", r"command not found",
    ]
    INPUT_ERROR_PATTERNS = [
        r"missing.*argument", r"required.*parameter",
        r"ambiguous", r"credential.*required",
    ]

    @classmethod
    def classify(cls, error: str) -> str:
        """Returns one of: 'model', 'tool', 'environment', 'input'"""
        error_lower = error.lower()
        for pattern in cls.INPUT_ERROR_PATTERNS:
            if re.search(pattern, error_lower):
                return "input"
        for pattern in cls.ENV_ERROR_PATTERNS:
            if re.search(pattern, error_lower):
                return "environment"
        for pattern in cls.TOOL_ERROR_PATTERNS:
            if re.search(pattern, error_lower):
                return "tool"
        return "model"  # default: model made a bad assumption
```

### Phase 2: Error-Aware Recovery

Modify the error handling in `handle_function_call()` or the tool result injection to:

- **model errors**: inject context hint ("the file you tried to patch does not contain the text you specified — re-read the file and verify the exact content")
- **tool errors**: exponential backoff retry (1s, 2s, 4s) before surfacing to LLM
- **environment errors**: hard stop, do not retry, report to user immediately
- **input errors**: ask user for clarification, do not retry

### Phase 3: Error State in Messages

Include the error type + recovery suggestion in the tool result message format so the LLM gets actionable guidance rather than a raw error string.

## Integration Points

- `run_agent.py` `handle_function_call()` — classify error before returning tool result
- `model_tools.py` `handle_function_call()` — add error classification wrapper
- `hermes_constants.py` — add `tool_error_retry_backoff` config option

## Value

- **Prevents stalls**: model errors escape the "retry the same thing" loop immediately
- **Saves tokens**: environment errors stop on first failure instead of wasting N retries
- **Better UX**: input errors prompt user instead of confusing retries
- **Complementary to stall detector**: error classification prevents stalls, stall detector catches what slips through

## References

- Harness Engineering "8th sentence": "on failure -> identify failure type -> write to State -> choose recovery action"
- Existing `api_max_retries: 3` in config.yaml — API-level retry, no error type awareness
- `_detect_escape_drift` in `tools/fuzzy_match.py` — an existing domain-specific error classifier that could serve as pattern

items.title: Desktop dashboard serves HTTP 404 — dist/ packed into app.asar but never unpacked (asarUnpack missing dist/**)
items.body:
## Summary

On the packaged Hermes desktop app, the dashboard backend serves **HTTP 404 on all static routes** (`/`, `/assets`, `/health`) while API routes like `/login` return 200. Root cause: the desktop exports `HERMES_WEB_DIST` pointing at a path **inside `app.asar`** — an unservable location.

## Environment
- Hermes Agent core: **v0.16.0 (2026.6.5)**, upstream `fd4c8b40`
- Desktop app: **v0.15.1** (git-install release build, `apps/desktop/release/mac-arm64/`)
- OS: macOS (Apple Silicon), git-based install

## Symptoms
```
GET /        -> 404
GET /assets  -> 404
GET /health  -> 404
GET /login   -> 200   (API route — masks the issue)
```

## Root Cause

`resolveWebDist()` in `apps/desktop/electron/main.cjs` resolves via 3 tiers:
1. `HERMES_DESKTOP_WEB_DIST` env override
2. `app.asar.unpacked/dist` (the intended path)
3. Fallback: `app.asar/dist` — **inside the archive, not a real filesystem directory**

`build.asarUnpack` in `apps/desktop/package.json` is `["**/*.node", "**/prebuilds/**"]` — it does **not** include `dist/**`, so `app.asar.unpacked/dist` is never created. Tier 2 never matches → falls through to tier 3 (broken). This is related to the silent-404 failure already documented in #23817.

## Proposed Fix
Add `dist/**` to `asarUnpack`:
```json
"asarUnpack": ["**/*.node", "**/prebuilds/**", "dist/**"]
```
Also: harden `resolveWebDist()` tier-3 to detect when `APP_ROOT` is inside `.asar` and fail with a clear log message rather than silently returning an unservable path.

## Verified Workaround
Extract `dist/` from the asar to the expected unpacked location:
```bash
RES=".../Hermes.app/Contents/Resources"
TMP=$(mktemp -d)
npx --yes @electron/asar extract "$RES/app.asar" "$TMP/asar_full"
mkdir -p "$RES/app.asar.unpacked"
cp -R "$TMP/asar_full/dist" "$RES/app.asar.unpacked/dist"
rm -rf "$TMP"
```
After this, all static routes return 200. Lost on desktop re-package; the `asarUnpack` fix is durable.

## Impact
Any packaged install ships a non-functional dashboard. Severity: high. Discoverability: low (no error log; masked by stray CLI dashboard instances).

items.title: Desktop v0.15.1 probes /api/ws (WebSocket IPC bridge) which core v0.16.0 no longer serves → boot loop when launchd gateway is present

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Summary

The packaged desktop app cannot boot against the current core gateway. On launch the desktop's renderer opens a live WebSocket to `/api/ws` (its "IPC bridge"); the core gateway's `api_server` adapter is REST-only and exposes **no `/api/ws` route** (verified absent at repo HEAD `56236b16e`). The probe 404s → desktop shows **"Hermes couldn't start / Desktop IPC bridge is unavailable"** → falls back to spawning its own backend → collides with the always-on launchd gateway service → SIGTERM loop.

## Environment
- Core gateway: **v0.16.0 (2026.6.5)**, repo HEAD `56236b16e`
- Desktop app: **v0.15.1** (release build, `apps/desktop/release/mac-arm64/`)
- Always-on gateway: `~/Library/LaunchAgents/ai.hermes.gateway.plist` (KeepAlive + RunAtLoad)
- OS: macOS (Apple Silicon)

## Evidence
```bash
# Desktop expects a WebSocket IPC bridge:
# apps/desktop/electron/gateway-ws-probe.cjs:
#   "The RENDERER then opens a live WebSocket to /api/ws"

# Core api_server is REST-only — no ws route at runtime:
curl -i -H 'Connection: Upgrade' -H 'Upgrade: websocket' http://127.0.0.1:8642/api/ws  # -> 404
curl -s -o/dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:8642/api/health                  # -> 404
curl -s -o/dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:8642/health                       # -> 200

# No /api/ws anywhere in gateway/ at repo HEAD 56236b16e:
grep -rniE "'/api/ws'" gateway/   # -> (no matches)
```

Desktop boot log shows the loop:
```
[boot] Hermes backend is ready. Finalizing desktop startup
Hermes backend exited (SIGTERM)
[boot] Resolving Hermes backend ... (repeats)
```
The launchd-managed gateway (`gateway run --replace`, KeepAlive) holds :8642 and reclaims it each time the desktop spawns its own backend.

## Root Cause
Desktop↔core API contract drift: desktop v0.15.1 was built against a gateway that exposed a `/api/ws` WebSocket IPC bridge; core v0.16.0 refactored the API server to REST-only (streaming via `POST /api/sessions/{id}/chat/stream`) and removed the inbound `/api/ws` route. The launchd KeepAlive service (correct and expected behavior for 24/7 messaging/cron) turns the desktop's fallback self-spawn into a SIGTERM loop.

## Impact
Fresh desktop boots fail whenever desktop minor version lags core across this contract change. Everything else works (CLI, web dashboard, launchd gateway, messaging, cron) — blast radius is native desktop GUI only. Failure is opaque: a generic "couldn't start" screen with a Retry button that can never succeed since the endpoint doesn't exist.

## Proposed Fixes
1. **Version-gate**: surface a clear error ("desktop vX requires core ≥ vY — missing /api/ws") instead of a generic retry loop.
2. **Either** restore a `/api/ws` shim in `api_server` for backward compat, **or** update the desktop IPC bridge to the REST/stream contract (`POST /api/sessions/{id}/chat/stream`).
3. **Detect the launchd-vs-desktop gateway conflict**: if an external KeepAlive gateway already owns the API port, the desktop should attach to it rather than spawn-and-lose, and surface this clearly.

## Workaround
Use the web dashboard (`http://127.0.0.1:9120`) — the same SPA the desktop wraps, served by the dashboard backend, no `/api/ws` dependency. CLI, gateway, messaging, and cron are all unaffected.

### Problem or Use Case

Hermes auto-restarts cleanly (Docker `restart: unless-stopped`), but an unclean shutdown leaves no record of *why* it died. A native crash (GPU OOM, a segfault in a C extension, the OOM-killer) never surfaces a Python traceback, so the Docker/app logs just show the process vanishing and coming back. Recurring crashes are hard to diagnose — especially for anyone not watching logs live.


### Proposed Solution

A small, dependency-light crash_diagnostics module that reads the OS's own crash record and returns a normalized, human-readable cause + faulting backtrace:

macOS — ~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/*.ips · Linux — coredumpctl/journald · Windows — Application event log / WER via Get-WinEvent
GPU-aware (Metal/MLX on Apple, CUDA/NVIDIA on Linux/DGX), best-effort and fully wrapped so it can never raise into the caller. One call: recent_crashes(name_filter, since_hours) → [{when, process, signal, cause, backtrace}].

(real macOS example output — keep the code block from the saved draft)

This is core robustness infrastructure, not a skill — it runs automatically (e.g. on restart) and parses OS-level crash records precisely, in the same vein as the existing kanban_diagnostics, gateway diagnostics, and request_dump, rather than an LLM-invoked capability. items.body:
## Bug Description

When a user sends a video message to the Hermes Agent Telegram bot, the video file is downloaded and cached correctly by the Telegram adapter, but the cached path is never exposed to the AI agent. The agent only receives the text caption (if any) — it never sees the video path and therefore cannot use `vision_analyze` or `video_analyze` to process the video content.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Send a video message to a Hermes Agent bot on Telegram (with caption, e.g., "What's in this video?")
2. Observe the gateway logs — the video is cached at `~/.hermes/cache/videos/video_<uuid>.mp4`
3. Observe the agent's response — it cannot answer the question about the video because it never receives the video path

## Expected Behavior

The agent should receive the cached video path in its message context, similar to how documents and audio files are handled. For example:

```
[The user sent a video. It is saved at: /root/.hermes/cache/videos/video_xxx.mp4.
If you need to analyze it, use vision_analyze with image_url: /root/.hermes/cache/videos/video_xxx.mp4]

What's in this video?
```

## Actual Behavior

The agent receives only the text caption ("What's in this video?") without any indication that a video file was attached.

## Root Cause

In `gateway/run.py`, the `_process_message_background` method (around lines 8636–8651) dispatches incoming media attachments based on their type:

- **Images** (lines 8641–8676): `image/*` mime or `MessageType.PHOTO` → enriched with vision pre-analysis or attached natively
- **Voice messages** (lines 8647–8651): `MessageType.VOICE` → transcribed via STT
- **Audio files** (lines 8645–8646, 8713–8726): `MessageType.AUDIO` → path injected into message text
- **Documents** (lines 8728–8768): `MessageType.DOCUMENT` → path injected into message text

But **`MessageType.VIDEO` has no handling branch at all**. The video path in `event.media_urls` is silently ignored and never injected into the message text.

The Telegram adapter (`gateway/platforms/telegram.py`, line ~5504) correctly caches the video and populates `event.media_urls` and `event.media_types`, but there is no corresponding consumer downstream.

## Suggested Fix

Add a handling branch for `MessageType.VIDEO` (and/or `video/*` mime types) in the media dispatch section of `_process_message_background`, similar to how audio file attachments are handled — inject the cached video path into the message text so the agent can pass it to `vision_analyze` or `video_analyze`.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent version: current
- Platform adapter: Telegram
- OS: Linux

Even though `codex` is already installed at `~/.hermes/node/bin/codex` (Hermes's own bundled Node install, v0.137.0).

## Root Cause

macOS GUI apps launched via Launch Services inherit a **minimal PATH** (`/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin`), which does not include `~/.hermes/node/bin`. When the Electron desktop app spawns the Python dashboard process (`hermes dashboard`), this minimal PATH is passed through unchanged.

The `check_codex_binary()` function in `agent/transports/codex_app_server.py` calls `subprocess.run(["codex", "--version"])`, which searches PATH and fails with `FileNotFoundError`.

**Evidence from the running process:**

```
Dashboard PID: 30405  (ps eww $PID)
PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin
```

Same minimal PATH for the Electron parent process (PID 30401).

## Where the Fix Should Go

The Electron `main.cjs` already adds `~/.hermes/node/bin` to PATH for the **self-update** spawn path (line 1711–1716):

```js
const extraPath = [path.join(HERMES_HOME, 'node', 'bin'), path.join(updateRoot, 'venv', 'bin')]
  .filter(Boolean).join(path.delimiter)
const env = {
  HERMES_HOME,
  PATH: [extraPath, process.env.PATH].filter(Boolean).join(path.delimiter)
}
```

But the **dashboard spawn** (line 4501–4523) does NOT add this PATH extension — it just passes `...process.env` directly.

Alternatively, the Python side can fix this in `hermes_cli/main.py` — there is already near-identical PATH-extension logic in `_ensure_tui_node()` (lines 1480–1493) that prepends `~/.hermes/node/bin` to `os.environ["PATH"]`, but that function only runs for TUI mode, not for `hermes dashboard`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open Hermes desktop app on macOS
2. In any chat session, type `/codex-runtime on`
3. Observe the error: "codex CLI not found"

## Attempted Workarounds (all failed)

- `launchctl setenv PATH "..."` — does not propagate to GUI apps on modern macOS
- Modifying `Info.plist` `LSEnvironment` — breaks the app's code signature, prevents launch
- Symlink to `/usr/local/bin` — not in the GUI app's PATH

## Environment

- macOS 26.5.1 (Sequoia)
- Hermes desktop app (Electron, packaged)
- `codex-cli 0.137.0` at `~/.hermes/node/bin/codex` (working when invoked directly)
- `codex-cli 0.125.0` at `~/.local/share/fnm/...` (fnm-managed, also not in GUI PATH)

items.title: Bug: CLI/Desktop prompts can run live-only when state.db is unavailable

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
## Summary

Hermes can currently continue a normal CLI/Desktop prompt even when the SQLite session store is unavailable. That creates a live in-memory chat that appears healthy, but the transcript is not written to `state.db`, so Desktop/session resume later shows a truncated session.

## Real-world failure shape

Observed on macOS with a broken local checkout where `hermes_state.py` could not import:

```text
SQLite session store not available — session will NOT be indexed: invalid decimal literal (hermes_state.py, line 2068)
```

The agent then continued handling turns in memory. Later logs showed the same session had a large live history, but `state.db` only contained messages after the store recovered/restarted. Desktop therefore displayed the session starting from a later user message, making everything before it appear cut/lost.

## Why this is dangerous

- The user sees a normal chat UI/CLI session.
- The model still has live in-memory context, so the failure is not obvious during the run.
- The persisted transcript is incomplete or absent.
- After restart/resume, the session appears truncated.
- The only warning may be buried in logs.

## Expected behavior

Once a user submits a real prompt, Hermes should not silently run in live-only mode by default if session persistence is unavailable. It should either:

1. fail closed with a visible error before the agent starts, or
2. require an explicit unsafe/no-persistence opt-in.

`session.create` can stay lazy because no user transcript exists yet, but `prompt.submit` / CLI first prompt should not proceed as a normal saved chat if `state.db` cannot be opened or the initial session row cannot be persisted.

## Related work

Related but not identical:

- #8038 / #8061: append/flush failures after a SessionDB exists.
- #32805: fallback handling when `append_message()` fails after DB initialization.
- #29778: gateway DB-unavailable messaging / stale JSONL fallback contract.
- #30636: state.db corruption masking persistence loss.

This issue is the startup / pre-prompt variant: SessionDB is unavailable before the chat begins, but Hermes still lets a normal prompt run.

items.title: [Bug]: hermes cron list crashes with TypeError: can only join an iterable when any job has deliver: null

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
### Bug Description

`hermes cron list` raises an unhandled TypeError and lists no jobs if any job in `jobs.json` has deliver: null. `cron.py:95` does `", ".join(deliver)` assuming `deliver` is always an iterable of targets, but `None` is a valid stored value (jobs created without a delivery target persist `deliver: null`). One such job makes the entire `cron list` command unusable.

### Steps to Reproduce

- Have (or create) a cron job whose `deliver` ends up null in `jobs.json.` 
- Run `hermes cron list`.
- Observe the traceback above; no jobs listed.

### Expected Behavior

`cron list` should tolerate `deliver: null` (and ideally normalize string vs. list forms), e.g.:

```python
if not deliver:
    deliver_str = "—"        # or "(none)"
elif isinstance(deliver, str):
    deliver_str = deliver
else:
    deliver_str = ", ".join(deliver)
```
A malformed/empty delivery target on one job should not break listing of all jobs.

·## Notes
`deliver` appears to be typed/handled as a list at the display layer but stored as a scalar (`str` or `null`) at the job level. Worth reconciling the schema so creation and display agree on the type.

### Actual Behavior

`deliver` values in jobs.json are inconsistent across jobs — some are strings, some are `null`:

```
d68c2728b513 -> None   (NoneType)
a0c124e55b1f -> None   (NoneType)
09dd0c24f29b -> None   (NoneType)
3fae80a61126 -> 'whatsapp:+34XXXXXXXXX'  (str)
7fc40f2b1cef -> 'local'  (str)
```

### Affected Component

Configuration (config.yaml, .env, hermes setup), Agent Core (conversation loop, context compression, memory)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A (CLI only)

### Debug Report

```shell
Debug report uploaded:
  Report       https://paste.rs/bh7ws
  agent.log    https://paste.rs/EwkrE
  gateway.log  https://paste.rs/xPuBc
  desktop.log  https://paste.rs/QnFnZ
```

### Operating System

Ubuntu 24.04.2 LTS (GNU/Linux 6.6.87.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2 x86_64)

### Python Version

3.11.15

### Hermes Version

0.16.0

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../hermes_cli/main.py", line 16035, in main
    args.func(args)
  File ".../hermes_cli/main.py", line 6534, in cmd_cron
    cron_command(args)
  File ".../hermes_cli/cron.py", line 335, in cron_command
    cron_list(show_all)
  File ".../hermes_cli/cron.py", line 95, in cron_list
    deliver_str = ", ".join(deliver)
                  ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
TypeError: can only join an iterable
```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

`", ".join(deliver) at cron.py:95:`

- works on the string values (iterates char-by-char, no crash — though arguably also wrong, would render `l, o, c, a, l`),
- raises `TypeError` on `None`.

Since `cron_list` iterates over all jobs and hits the exception on the first `None`, the whole command fails and zero jobs are displayed, even the well-formed ones.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Minimal — close the `None` gap in the default fallback that's already there. Change the `.get()` default to an `or`, so a present-but-null value also falls back to the default:

```
deliver = job.get("deliver") or ["local"]   # was: job.get("deliver", ["local"])
if isinstance(deliver, str):
    deliver = [deliver]
deliver_str = ", ".join(deliver)
```

`job.get("deliver") or ["local"]` routes `None`, `""`, and `[]` to the default, while the existing `isinstance(str)` branch keeps handling single/comma-separated string targets (`deliver` is multi-target by design, see #11602). One line, consistent with the current style, and stops one null-deliver job from breaking `cron list` for all jobs — including pre-existing jobs.json data that already contains deliver: null.

## Notes (separate, lower priority)

The display fix above stops the crash for existing data. The deeper inconsistency is on the write side: `cron_add`/`cron_update` (around `cron.py:218` and `:284`) persist `deliver=getattr(args, "deliver", None)`, which is how `deliver: null` ends up in` jobs.json` in the first place. Normalizing `deliver` to a canonical shape at write time (default or empty list rather than `None`) would stop the inconsistency being written at all. That's a separate, smaller cleanup — not required to fix this crash, and probably its own issue/PR.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [x] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

items.title: Security scanner (Tirith) SIGSEGV crash causes 20-minute agent hang with no response delivery

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
## Summary

The Tirith security scanner crashes with SIGSEGV (exit code -11) on every tool invocation when `tirith_path` points to a non-existent binary. Combined with the agent's retry loop, this caused a 20-minute hang where zero responses were delivered to the user despite continuous API calls.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.14.0 (2026.5.16)
- Providers: deepseek-v4-flash (triggering task), qwen3.6-plus (recovery)
- Platform: Feishu (Lark)
- Config: `tirith_enabled: true`, `tirith_path: "tirith"`, `tirith_fail_open: true`
- `tirith` binary: NOT installed (`which tirith` returns empty, no pip package)

## Impact

- 2,704+ Tirith crashes over 7 days (hidden behind `fail_open: true`)
- Agent stuck for ~20 minutes (2026-06-08 00:00-00:20) with NO response delivered
- 3 user messages received but never answered during the hang

## Root Cause

### 1. Tirith binary not found → SIGSEGV (Chronic)
`config.yaml` sets `tirith_path: "tirith"` but the binary doesn't exist. Every tool invocation triggers:
```
tools.tirith_security: tirith returned unexpected exit code -11
```
Exit code -11 = SIGSEGV. Hidden for 7 days because `tirith_fail_open: true` lets tools proceed despite the crash.

### 2. Agent retry loop deadlock (Acute)
A multi-file patch task entered a failure→retry cycle:
- `patch` returns "Found 2 matches for old_string" 
- Model retries with slightly different old_string → same error
- Cycle repeats across multiple files for ~20 min
- No turn completion → no response flushed to Feishu

### 3. No per-turn timeout / circuit breaker
- No max tool-call budget per turn
- No timeout after which agent must respond or abort
- Subsequent user messages queued but unanswered

## Evidence

```
2026-06-08 00:00:36 inbound message: msg='按这个执行吧。'
2026-06-08 00:00:42 tirith returned unexpected exit code -11  ← first crash
2026-06-08 00:01:03 patch error: "Found 2 matches for old_string"
2026-06-08 00:08:08 inbound message: msg='还在执行吗？'  ← no response
2026-06-08 00:09:26 inbound message: msg='暂停'  ← no response
# No "response ready" entries from 00:00:36 to ~00:20
```

## Recommended Fixes

1. **Startup validation**: Verify `tirith_path` resolves to an executable; auto-disable or fail-fast if missing
2. **Circuit breaker for security tools**: After N consecutive failures, skip scanning with a warning
3. **Per-turn timeout / max tool budget**: Force response after timeout, don't let retry loops run indefinitely
4. **Response delivery for long turns**: Send "still working" status updates or flush partial responses
5. **Patch tool improvement**: When "Found N matches" error, provide the matching lines with context so the model can disambiguate

## Files to Review
- `tools/tirith_security.py`
- `agent/tool_executor.py`
- `agent/conversation_loop.py`
- `gateway/run.py`
- `gateway/platforms/feishu.py`

items.title: [Feature] WhatsApp: send_message media attachment support (bridge already exposes /send-media)

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Summary

`tools/send_message_tool.py` implements media (image/video/audio/document) delivery for matrix, signal, telegram, discord, weixin, yuanbao, and feishu — but **not WhatsApp**, even though the bundled Baileys bridge (`scripts/whatsapp-bridge/bridge.js`) already exposes a `/send-media` endpoint that handles all four media types natively (with auto-detection from file extension and ffmpeg-based ogg/opus conversion for voice).

The Python side just never calls it. Any `send_message` call with `media_files` to a WhatsApp chat hits the "Non-media platforms" fallback, which returns:

```
send_message MEDIA delivery is currently only supported for telegram, discord, matrix, weixin, signal, yuanbao and feishu
```

The text portion goes through `/send`; the attachment is silently dropped.

## Repro

```python
result = await send_message_tool.run(
    target_ref="whatsapp:<groupjid>@g.us",
    message="Here's the PDF\nMEDIA:/tmp/report.pdf",
)
# → text sent, MEDIA stripped, warning returned about WhatsApp not supporting media
```

## Bridge capability (already there)

`bridge.js` lines exposing the endpoint, in case it's not obvious from a quick read:

```js
 *   POST /send-media     - Send media natively { chatId, filePath, mediaType?, caption?, fileName? }

app.post('/send-media', async (req, res) => {
    ...
    const { chatId, filePath, mediaType, caption, fileName } = req.body;
    ...
    const type = mediaType || inferMediaType(ext);   // image | video | audio | document
    ...
});
```

Auto-detects type by extension, handles ogg/opus voice conversion via ffmpeg, supports captions.

## Proposed fix

Mirror the Signal/Matrix/Feishu pattern in `_send_to_platform`:

```python
# --- WhatsApp: native media via Baileys bridge /send-media endpoint ---
if platform == Platform.WHATSAPP and media_files:
    last_result = None
    for i, chunk in enumerate(chunks):
        is_last = (i == len(chunks) - 1)
        result = await _send_whatsapp(
            pconfig.extra, chat_id, chunk,
            media_files=media_files if is_last else [],
        )
        if isinstance(result, dict) and result.get("error"):
            return result
        last_result = result
    return last_result
```

Plus extend `_send_whatsapp` to accept `media_files=None`, send text via `/send` as today, then POST each file to `/send-media`. Update the two fallback error/warning messages to list whatsapp.

Patch is ~30 lines total. Backward-compatible (the new kwarg defaults to None; existing call sites unaffected). Happy to send a PR — same shape as #40874, #41331, #41340.

## Local workaround

Patch script applying these changes deployed to our agents until upstream merges. Marker: `# HERMES_PATCH_WHATSAPP_MEDIA`.

## Version

`main` branch as of 2026-06-07.

items.title: [Bug] send_message WhatsApp targets: group/LID JIDs silently fall back to home channel

labels.name: sweeper:cannot-reproduce
labels.description: Sweeper: could not reproduce on current main

items.body:
## Summary

`tools/send_message_tool.py::_parse_target_ref` mis-routes WhatsApp targets in two related ways:

1. **JID targets fall through silently** — `<digits>@g.us` (group), `<digits>@s.whatsapp.net` (DM full form), `<digits>@lid` (LID) aren't recognized; `_parse_target_ref` returns `(None, None, False)` and the caller routes to the home channel.

2. **Bare-digit targets crash the bridge** — `whatsapp:120363022690908060` (just digits, no JID suffix) DOES get accepted by the generic `target_ref.lstrip("-").isdigit()` branch and passed straight through to the Baileys bridge, which calls `jidDecode("120363022690908060")` and gets `undefined` back, then crashes with:

   ```
   Cannot destructure property 'user' of 'jidDecode(...)' as it is undefined.
   ```

Both bugs surface for the same reason: `_parse_target_ref` is built around E.164 phone numbers and doesn't know that WhatsApp identifiers can also be group IDs (17+ digits) or LIDs.

## Repro

### Case 1 — suffixed JID falls to home channel

```python
result = await send_message_tool.run(
    target_ref="whatsapp:120363022690908060@g.us",
    message="hello group",
)
# → returns success: True, but chat_id is the home DM (13174278802@s.whatsapp.net),
#   NOT the requested group.
```

### Case 2 — bare digits crash the bridge

```python
result = await send_message_tool.run(
    target_ref="whatsapp:120363022690908060",
    message="hello group",
)
# → returns {"error": "WhatsApp bridge error (500): {\"error\":\"Cannot destructure
#   property 'user' of 'jidDecode(...)' as it is undefined.\"}"}
```

Net effect: there is no canonical way to send to a WhatsApp group via send_message in stock hermes — bare digits crash, suffixed JIDs silently misroute. Same for LIDs.

## Root cause

`_parse_target_ref` lines around the WhatsApp branch:

```python
if platform_name in _PHONE_PLATFORMS:   # {"signal", "sms", "whatsapp"}
    match = _E164_TARGET_RE.fullmatch(target_ref)
    if match:
        return target_ref.strip(), None, True
# ... falls through to:
if target_ref.lstrip("-").isdigit():
    return target_ref, None, True   # accepts bare digits, but bridge can't decode them
# ... else:
return None, None, False             # JIDs end up here → caller routes to home
```

`_E164_TARGET_RE` is for `+15551234567`-shape numbers. The generic all-digits fallback was intended for Telegram chat IDs, where bare digits ARE valid, but for WhatsApp it produces invalid input for the bridge.

## Proposed fix (~12 lines)

Add a WhatsApp-specific branch in `_parse_target_ref` that handles both forms before the `_PHONE_PLATFORMS` check:

```python
if platform_name == "whatsapp":
    candidate = target_ref.strip()
    # Suffixed JIDs: <digits>@g.us, <digits>@s.whatsapp.net, <digits>@lid
    if re.fullmatch(r"\d+@(g\.us|s\.whatsapp\.net|lid)", candidate):
        return candidate, None, True
    # Bare digits — auto-classify by length. 17+ digits → group ID,
    # 7-15 digits → phone number (E.164 max is 15). 16 is ambiguous;
    # leave it for the existing all-digits branch to handle.
    bare = candidate.lstrip("+")
    if bare.isdigit():
        if len(bare) >= 17:
            return f"{bare}@g.us", None, True
        if 7 <= len(bare) <= 15:
            return f"{bare}@s.whatsapp.net", None, True
```

E.164 phone targets continue to work (the bare-digits branch now produces the proper `@s.whatsapp.net` form which Baileys handles directly). Existing call sites unaffected.

Optional sweetener while here: when the bridge gets a malformed JID, return `"chatId '%s' is not a valid WhatsApp JID — expected <digits>@g.us, <digits>@s.whatsapp.net, <digits>@lid, or a bare E.164 phone"` instead of letting the destructure crash propagate. Took us a while to figure out the bridge was failing on jidDecode rather than something hermes-side. (`scripts/whatsapp-bridge/bridge.js`, `/send` and `/send-media` route handlers.)

Also: consider logging a `logger.warning(...)` when `_parse_target_ref` returns False and the caller falls back to home_chat. Silent home-channel fallback is the friction that made (1) hard to diagnose in the first place.

Happy to send a PR. Same shape as #40874 / #41331 / #41340 / #41405.

## Local workaround

Two patch scripts deployed to our agents until upstream merges:
- `# HERMES_PATCH_WHATSAPP_JID_TARGET` — suffixed JID recognizer (case 1)
- `# HERMES_PATCH_WHATSAPP_BARE_DIGITS` — bare-digit normalization (case 2)

Combined: ~25 lines. Verified end-to-end: PDF + caption to an 18-digit group ID lands in the group via the bridge's `/send-media` endpoint (per #41405's fix).

## Version

`main` branch as of 2026-06-07.
